title: Automated urine analysis of atypical urothelial cells for urothelial carcinoma: a prospective study.
abstract: Objectives To prospectively evaluate the diagnostic value of atypical urothelial cells (Atyp.C), an automatically determined quantitative parameter of the Sysmex UF-5000 urine particle analyser (Sysmex Corp., Kobe, Japan), as a non-invasive biomarker for urothelial carcinoma (UC). Early diagnosis of UC remains challenging despite advances in diagnostic techniques. While non-invasive urine cytology has high diagnostic value, clinical evidence for Atyp.C in urine remains unclear. Quantification of Atyp.C in urine may improve non-invasive UC disease diagnostics. Patients and methods Urine samples from 234 patients who underwent invasive urological intervention for non-malignant conditions (control group [CG]) or UC (intervention group [IG]) were considered. Based on histopathology, the IG was subclassified into low-grade (LG) and high-grade (HG) UC and was further grouped into non-muscle-invasive (non-MI) and MI UC. Patients who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy were analysed separately. Atyp.C of ≥0.1 Atyp.C/μL were defined as positive and were automatically quantified using the Sysmex UF-5000 urine particle analyser, which classifies epithelial cells with disproportionately high nucleic acid content relative to cell size. Smoking state, urinary tract infection (UTI), and micro-/macrohaematuria, were evaluated as potential confounding factors. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess explorative diagnostic Atyp.C performance. Results The Atyp.C concentration was higher in the IG than in the CG (mean [SEM] 0.53 [0.1] vs 0.29 [0.1] Atyp.C/μL; P = 0.004), with a sensitivity of 0.59. HGUC exhibited higher Atyp.C levels (mean [SEM] 0.85 [0.2] Atyp.C/μL, P < 0.001) and a sensitivity of 0.73. MI UC showed the highest Atyp.C concentrations (mean [SEM] 0.95 [0.4] Atyp.C/μL; P = 0.004) and sensitivity of 0.78. ROC analysis demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy for MI UC (area under the ROC curve = 0.75). ROC analysis was exploratory and lacked external validation. UTI was a significant confounder for Atyp.C quantification. Conclusion The Atyp.C are elevated in HGUC, particularly in MI disease, supporting their potential as a non-invasive diagnostic biomarker in UC condition.

title: Longitudinal genital growth curves in adolescents and Doppler-based varicocele risk stratification.
abstract: Objectives To construct longitudinal ultrasound-based growth curves for genital development and to assess the prognostic value of varicocele grade and Doppler features. Varicoceles affect ~20% of adolescent boys and can be associated with impaired fertility. Evidence-based criteria for intervention are lacking due to limited longitudinal data. Subjects, patients and methods We conducted a prospective longitudinal cohort study (2015-2021) of 570 boys aged 10.5-18 years (407 controls, 163 with left-sided varicocele; 1352 assessments). The boys underwent Tanner pubic hair staging (TSP), measurement of stretched penile length (SPL), and a scrotal ultrasound. The volumes of the left and right testes and total testicular volume (TTV) were calculated according to the Lambert formula. In varicocele, venous diameter (VD), spontaneous reflux (SR), peak retrograde flow (PRF), and clinical grade were measured. Growth trajectories were analysed using mixed-effects models. Results Severe subgroups (VD ≥3 mm, SR >20 cm/s, or Grade 3) had attenuated growth slopes and lower TTV at TSP 5 vs controls. Combined risk profiles (e.g., Grade 3 + VD ≥3 mm; SR >20 cm/s + Grade 3) showed the poorest outcomes, with final TTV consistently <30 mL. A PRF >38.4 cm/s alone was not predictive. The SPL differences were minimal. Some subgroups entered puberty earlier but progressed more slowly. Limitations include absence of semen and hormonal data, exclusion of atypical developmental disorders, and limited ethnic diversity. Conclusions Most adolescents with a varicocele develop normally. Only those with combined high-risk Doppler and clinical features show impaired testicular growth. Doppler adds prognostic value beyond grade and supports a stratified surveillance strategy, potentially reducing overtreatment.

title: DFDBA With or Without Platelet-Rich Fibrin in Maxillary Sinus Augmentation: A Randomized Split-Mouth Clinical Trial.
abstract: Objectives To compare histologic and histomorphometric outcomes after bilateral lateral maxillary sinus augmentation with demineralized freeze-dried bone allograft (DFDBA) alone versus DFDBA combined with platelet-rich fibrin (PRF), and to report 1-year prosthetic follow-up of the restored implants. Materials and methods This randomized split-mouth clinical trial included subjects requiring bilateral lateral maxillary sinus augmentation before implant placement. In each subject, one sinus was randomly assigned to DFDBA alone and the contralateral sinus to DFDBA combined with leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF) and injectable PRF (i-PRF). Bone biopsy specimens were harvested at the clinically relevant 6-month implant placement time point. The primary outcome was newly formed bone. Secondary histomorphometric outcomes were residual graft material, connective tissue, and fibrosis; inflammation and necrosis were assessed histologically. Clinical and radiographic prosthetic follow-up was performed 1 year after definitive prosthetic loading. Paired comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Results Of 24 enrolled subjects, 21 completed follow-up and contributed 42 sinus sites to the paired analysis. Median newly formed bone was 48.72% (IQR, 33.33%-63.33%) on the PRF side and 45.76% (IQR, 37.14%-54.90%) on the non-PRF side (p = 0.5). Residual graft material was 6.74% versus 4.23% (p = 0.2), connective tissue was 31.48% versus 36.92% (p = 0.016), and fibrosis was 3.42% versus 2.56% (p > 0.9). No inflammation or necrosis was observed. Following replacement of one implant that failed before prosthetic loading, all definitively restored implants remained functional during the 1-year prosthetic follow-up. Clinical and radiographic follow-up was uneventful, and no biologic or prosthetic complications requiring intervention were observed. Conclusions Adding PRF to DFDBA did not significantly increase newly formed bone at the 6-month implant placement time point. The lower connective tissue proportion on the PRF side may suggest altered tissue maturation; however, this secondary finding should be interpreted cautiously. Definitively restored implants showed 100% prosthetic survival during 1-year follow-up. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07348198; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07348198. This clinical trial was not registered prior to participant recruitment and randomization.

title: Fully automated AI-based quantification of tumour volume on PSMA PET-CT images is associated with overall survival in prostate cancer.
abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI)-based models can quantify tumour volume in positron emission tomography (PET) examinations using prostate specific membrane antigen (PSMA). It is, however, unknown whether this measurement of tumour volume contains prognostic information. The purpose of this study was to examine whether tumour volume measured by AI is associated with overall survival in patients with prostate cancer. Methods Patients who had undergone [ 18 F]PSMA-1007 PET-CT due to primary staging or biochemical recurrence (BCR) of prostate cancer at our centre were retrospectively included and followed for 5 years. Automatic quantification of tumour volume was performed using a previously developed fully automated AI model from our research group for PSMA PET-CT analysis, without manual corrections. The tumour volume for the prostate, lymph nodes, and bone was calculated and summarized as Total Lesion Volume (TLV) and divided categorically (no detectable tumour, low, and high) as well as aggregated to whole-body TLV and divided into tertiles (low, intermediate, and high). Mortality rates were compared using Cox-regression and adjusted for age. Results Among 267 patients in the final analysis, 48 (18%) died during follow-up. Whole-body TLV was significantly associated with mortality in the combined cohort (p = 0.001) and in the primary staging cohort (p = 0.014) but did not reach statistical significance in the BCR cohort (p = 0.061). Conclusions Fully automated AI-derived TLV from PSMA PET-CT was associated with overall survival. These findings support the potential role of AI-based tumour quantification as a potential prognostic biomarker in prostate cancer.

title: Bias-Controlled Quantitative Analysis of Golgi-Stained Neurons via High-Fidelity Denoising.
abstract: Quantitative analysis of Golgi-stained neurons is fundamentally limited by non-specific precipitates that introduce substantial bias into morphological measurements. Conventional denoising approaches, designed mainly for low-resolution medical imaging or reconstruction artefacts, are insufficient for suppressing this chemically induced noise at sub-micrometre resolution. Here, we present a high-fidelity denoising strategy for Golgi-stained neurons (HiFi Golgi), a bias-controlled analytical strategy for three-dimensional (3D) Golgi-stained neuronal imaging. We established a multidimensional evaluation framework to systematically quantify the trade-off between noise suppression and structural fidelity, enabling rigorous comparison of candidate filtering strategies. Using this framework, an optimised low-parameter bilateral filter was identified that minimises noise-induced bias while preserving neuronal morphology. The HiFi Golgi strategy consistently reduces bias across diverse brain regions, imaging resolutions, and model species without parameter re-optimization, improving the reliability and reproducibility of single-neuron reconstruction. This work provides a generalizable and high-fidelity analytical approach for bias-controlled volumetric imaging, offering a reproducible framework for quantitative morphological analysis in complex neuronal systems.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Intraoperative Imprint Cytology and Frozen Section in Ovarian Tumours: Experience From a Tertiary Care Centre in Montenegro.
abstract: Objective Intraoperative assessment of ovarian tumours is crucial for surgical decision-making, especially regarding extent of resection and fertility preservation. Frozen section is standard, while imprint cytology is a potential alternative method. The aim was to evaluate and compare the diagnostic accuracy of imprint cytology and frozen section in ovarian tumours using final histopathology as the reference standard in this study. Methods This retrospective study included 29 consecutive patients with ovarian masses operated at a tertiary care centre in Montenegro during 2023-2024. All cases were evaluated intraoperatively using both imprint cytology and frozen section. Final histopathological diagnosis on paraffin-embedded sections, classified according to WHO 2020 criteria, served as reference standard. Archival material was reviewed independently by two pathologists blinded to final diagnosis; discrepancies were resolved by consensus. Statistical analysis included sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, accuracy, and correlation testing using chi-square test and Spearman correlation with p < 0.05 significant. Results Imprint cytology correctly classified 28/29 cases, yielding an overall diagnostic accuracy of 96.6%. Sensitivity was 100% for benign and borderline tumours and 80% for malignant tumours. Frozen section correctly classified 26/29 cases, with an overall accuracy of 89.7%; sensitivity was 100% for benign, 50% for borderline and 60% for malignant tumours. Agreement with final histopathology was higher for imprint cytology (κ = 0.907) than for frozen section (κ = 0.704). The difference in overall accuracy was not statistically significant (McNemar p = 0.500). Conclusion Imprint cytology demonstrated promising diagnostic performance and may represent a useful adjunct or alternative to frozen section, particularly in resource-limited settings. Larger prospective multicentre studies are required to validate these findings.

title: Early Changes in Peripancreatic Mesenteric Fat Beyond Weight Loss Predict Durability of Hepatic Improvements in MASLD.
abstract: Aims Various visceral adipose tissue depots exhibit heterogeneous metabolic properties. This study aims to explore whether specific abdominal fat compartments differentially predict loss of sustained treatment response to lifestyle interventions in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Materials and methods Consecutive treatment-naïve MASLD patients were prospectively enrolled from January 2015 to March 2024, with a 96-week follow-up period. Liver fat content, preperitoneal fat thickness (PFT), peripancreatic mesenteric fat thickness (MFT1), periumbilical mesenteric fat thickness (MFT2) and perirenal fat thickness (PrFT) were quantified using magnetic resonance imaging. Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) was assessed by 2D-SWE. Treatment responses were evaluated at 48 and 96 weeks, and the primary outcome was loss of response at 96 weeks. Results A total of 631 MASLD patients (mean age: 41.5 ± 13.8 years; 72.0% male) were included. Logistic regression analyses revealed that a greater 48-week relative decrease in MFT1 (per 10% relative reduction), rather than in MFT2, PFT or PrFT, was independently associated with lower odds of losing MRI-PDFF response (OR: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.34-0.69, p < 0.001) and LSM response (OR: 0.53, 95% CI: 0.28-0.99, p = 0.046) at 96 weeks. Receiver operating characteristic curve analyses indicated that relative changes in MFT1 showed discriminatory ability for the loss of MRI-PDFF and LSM responses, with areas under the curves of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.64-0.76) and 0.77 (95% CI: 0.67-0.88), respectively. Conclusions Early changes in MFT1 were associated with subsequent loss of response in hepatic steatosis and fibrosis, suggesting potential prognostic value for hepatic response durability in MASLD.

title: Cognitive Cerebellum Structure and Functional Connectivity in Relation to Executive Functions in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
abstract: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) has been primarily linked to abnormalities within the cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuit; however, recent evidence suggests that the posterior cerebellum may contribute to the executive dysfunction observed in the disorder. In 56 adults (28 OCD, 28 controls), we assessed executive functions using the BANFE-2 battery and integrated structural MRI (T1) and resting-state fMRI. Although the Global Executive Index did not differ significantly between groups, patients with OCD showed significantly lower scores in the inhibitory control/decision-making domain relative to controls. We quantified cortical thickness and volume (% intracranial volume) in Crus I/II and lobule VI using CERES and examined resting-state functional connectivity (seed-to-voxel) in CONN, adjusting for age, sex, medication, and depression. Compared with controls, patients with OCD showed reduced bilateral cortical thickness in Crus I/II and lobule VI (false discovery rate-corrected q < 0.05; β_OCD - Control = -0.27 to -0.59; ηp 2 = 0.34-0.55), with no significant volumetric differences after correction for multiple comparisons. Functional connectivity results revealed a mixed pattern, including focal hyperconnectivity (e.g., left Crus I with primary auditory cortex; left Crus II with occipital cortex) and widespread intracerebellar hypoconnectivity. In addition, significant Group × executive-function interactions (p-family-wise error < 0.05) emerged mainly for bilateral Crus I (Global Executive Index and working memory/flexibility) and left lobule VI (inhibition/decision-making), indicating that the relationship between cerebellar connectivity and executive performance differs in OCD relative to controls. These findings support an expanded model of executive circuits in OCD that incorporates the posterior cerebellum as a relevant node.

title: Convergence of Cerebrospinal Fluid Neuronal Biomarker Burden and MRI Lesion Pattern and Its Association With Short-Term Outcome in Neuroinfectious Diseases.
abstract: Background Neuroinfectious diseases (NDs) are potentially treatable conditions associated with substantial morbidity, but their clinical course remains difficult to predict. While specific MRI patterns are characteristic of distinct aetiologies, their prognostic value remains poorly investigated. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers of neuroaxonal and synaptic damage have been linked to clinical outcome. We investigated the association of CSF biomarkers and MRI findings with short-term outcome in NDs. Methods In this multicentre cohort study, CSF was analysed in 123 patients with NDs and in 95 non-neuroinflammatory controls. Concentrations of beta-synuclein, SNAP-25, neurogranin and neurofilament light chain protein (NfL) were measured. MRI findings were classified by topography and lesion pattern. Clinical outcome at discharge was assessed using the modified Rankin Scale and degree of recovery. Results All CSF biomarkers were higher in ND patients with MRI abnormalities than in those without MRI abnormalities and/or controls, also within the (meningo-)encephalitis group. Temporal lobe involvement was the MRI pattern most consistently associated with elevated CSF biomarkers, even after multivariable adjustment including aetiology, and was independently associated with poor functional outcome and incomplete recovery. A global neuronal biomarker burden derived by principal component analysis (PC1) improved the fit of outcome models including MRI lesion pattern, with both temporal lobe involvement and PC1 remaining independently associated with outcome at discharge. Conclusions MRI lesion pattern and CSF biomarkers of synaptic and neuroaxonal damage were independently associated with short-term outcome in NDs, suggesting that they capture complementary aspects of disease severity. Prospective studies are needed to establish their prognostic value.

title: The CoMPaSS-NMD Atlas Platform: A Secure Multimodal Infrastructure for Harmonized Data Collection, Exploration, and Future Artificial Intelligence-Driven Stratification in Hereditary Neuromuscular Disorders.
abstract: Background Hereditary neuromuscular disorders exhibit marked phenotypic and molecular heterogeneity, which weakens genotype-phenotype correlation and complicates timely diagnosis, prognosis, and patient stratification for clinical trials. The Horizon Europe project CoMPaSS-NMD aims to develop artificial-intelligence-based stratification tools by integrating clinical, genetic, histopathological, and imaging data from clinical reference centers across Europe and the United Kingdom. Methods We developed CoMPaSS-NMD Atlas, a secure, modular web platform for pseudonymized data collection, multimodal data management, and controlled exploration. Clinical, technical, and data-management experts defined requirements; contributing centers co-designed electronic clinical and histopathology forms. Clinical phenotypes used the Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO), while imaging, histopathology, and sequencing data followed international standards. Results The platform supports role- and attribute-based access, pseudonymized patient registration, metadata management, structured clinical data entry, MRI and histopathological uploads, and a dedicated genetic-sequencing workflow. Cohort-level exploration is driven by structured metadata and HPO terms, enabling hierarchical phenotype navigation, ontology-aware data navigation, and cross-domain queries spanning clinical, genetic, imaging, and histopathological features. Users can download raw files in their original formats, along with structured metadata reports in CSV or PDF, according to the permissions defined for data protection. Conclusions The Atlas provides a foundation for harmonized, standardized prospective data collection and for building large datasets for artificial intelligence- and machine learning-based patient stratification. With secure governance, traceability, and multimodal integration, it is designed to support diagnostic and stratification research in hereditary neuromuscular disorders; clinical validation is ongoing.

title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to conventional oral photographs for recognition, classification, localization, segmentation, and risk assessment of oral mucosal lesions. This systematic review evaluated how clinically relevant visual information-including color, texture, morphology, borders, and spatial patterns-is represented by AI systems and assessed performance, validation, explainability, human comparison, and clinical translation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies directly analyzing conventional white-light clinical photographs. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation-based approaches. Fifty-three studies were included, 30 published in 2025-2026. Forty-six used implicit deep-learning visual representations, three multimodal vision-language models, two explicit color analyses, and two explicit texture analyses. Thirty-one studies primarily addressed image-level diagnostic classification/recognition, 15 spatial detection/localization or lesion delineation, six screening/triage/referral or biopsy-oriented decision support, and one longitudinal malignant-transformation prediction. Six used independent external cohorts and five compared AI with human readers. Methodological concerns were frequent, no sufficiently coherent group supported meta-analysis, and certainty remained limited across evidence bodies. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, with translation requiring stronger patient-level independence, external validation, prospective multicenter evaluation, and evidence of clinical benefit.

title: CDKN1A Mediates Regulated Cell Death in Osteoblasts and Exacerbates Periapical Bone Destruction in Apical Periodontitis.
abstract: Background Apical periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory bone-destructive disease driven by intracanal microbial infection and host immune-inflammatory responses. Periapical bone destruction arises not only from excessive osteoclastic resorption but also from osteoblast dysfunction and dysregulated regulated cell death (RCD). CDKN1A (p21) is a canonical cell-cycle regulator implicated in multiple RCD programs, yet its role in osteoblast injury and apical periodontitis pathogenesis remains undefined. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing (ScRNA) was used to profile osteoblast subpopulations and RCD-related gene expression in human periapical lesions. Porphyromonas gingivalis infection models were established in MG63 and MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts, and DIA proteomics and western blot were used to evaluate RCD-related proteins. The effects of CDKN1A, a disease-associated hub gene screened out in DIA proteomics, on RCD-related proteins were further examined by western blot. Lentiviral silencing and AAV-mediated overexpression were performed in vitro and in rat apical periodontitis models. Bone destruction, RCD activation and osteogenic capacity were assessed by micro-CT, histomorphology and multiplex immunofluorescence. Results ScRNA data of apical periodontitis showed that osteoblasts in apical lesions exhibited enhanced apoptosis and pyroptosis and reduced ferroptosis. Single-bacteria P. gingivalis infection markedly upregulated CDKN1A, which promoted osteoblast apoptosis and pyroptosis while suppressing necroptosis and ferroptosis. In vivo, CDKN1A expression increased with disease progression and was negatively correlated with the osteogenic marker OPN. CDKN1A overexpression aggravated bone destruction, whereas its knockdown significantly attenuated bone loss and restored osteogenic activity. Conclusion CDKN1A acts as a critical regulator that mediates RCD of osteoblasts, impairs osteogenesis and exacerbates periapical bone destruction in apical periodontitis. Targeting CDKN1A-mediated RCD represents a promising therapeutic strategy to limit bone destruction and promote repair in apical periodontitis.

Single-cell RNA sequencing (ScRNA) was used to profile osteoblast subpopulations and RCD-related gene expression in human periapical lesions. Porphyromonas gingivalis infection models were established in MG63 and MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts, and DIA proteomics and western blot were used to evaluate RCD-related proteins. The effects of CDKN1A, a disease-associated hub gene screened out in DIA proteomics, on RCD-related proteins were further examined by western blot. Lentiviral silencing and AAV-mediated overexpression were performed in vitro and in rat apical periodontitis models. Bone destruction, RCD activation and osteogenic capacity were assessed by micro-CT, histomorphology and multiplex immunofluorescence.

Results

ScRNA data of apical periodontitis showed that osteoblasts in apical lesions exhibited enhanced apoptosis and pyroptosis and reduced ferroptosis. Single-bacteria P. gingivalis infection markedly upregulated CDKN1A, which promoted osteoblast apoptosis and pyroptosis while suppressing necroptosis and ferroptosis. In vivo, CDKN1A expression increased with disease progression and was negatively correlated with the osteogenic marker OPN. CDKN1A overexpression aggravated bone destruction, whereas its knockdown significantly attenuated bone loss and restored osteogenic activity.

Conclusion

CDKN1A acts as a critical regulator that mediates RCD of osteoblasts, impairs osteogenesis and exacerbates periapical bone destruction in apical periodontitis. Targeting CDKN1A-mediated RCD represents a promising therapeutic strategy to limit bone destruction and promote repair in apical periodontitis.

title: Clinical Diagnosis Versus Plain Radiography for Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis: A Prospective Study of Diagnostic Agreement in a Resource-Limited Settings.
abstract: Diabetic foot osteomyelitis (DFO) is a serious complication of diabetic foot ulcers, particularly in advanced infections. In low-resource settings, access to medical imaging may be limited. This study evaluated the diagnostic agreement between a composite clinical approach (clinical assessment plus probe-to-bone test) compared with plain radiography for diagnosing DFO, including performance across ulcer categories. A prospective cohort study was conducted from December 2021 to January 2025 among patients with suspected DFO. Participants underwent clinical evaluation, risk factor assessment, ulcer history, SINBAD classification, probe-to-bone testing and plain radiography. Diagnostic performance measures were calculated. Given the absence of a gold standard reference test (bone biopsy) in this low-resource setting, performance measures represent comparative diagnostic agreement with plain radiography rather than absolute diagnostic accuracy. A total of 166 patients with deep foot ulcers were enrolled. Composite clinical diagnosis identified osteomyelitis in 117 patients and excluded it in 49. Plain radiography was positive in 96 of 117 composite positive cases, while 21 were discordant; all 49 composite negative cases were radiographically negative. The composite approach showed 100% sensitivity, 70% specificity and 87.3% overall agreement. Sensitivity remained 100% across ulcer categories, while specificity increased significantly from 63.8% in SINBAD-4 ulcers to 77.8% in SINBAD-5 ulcers, improving agreement from 86.1% to 89.7%. In conclusion, composite clinical diagnosis demonstrates substantial agreement with plain radiography in this cohort of patients with suspected DFO. This can provide a practical adjunct for clinical assessment in resource-limited settings where imaging is unavailable or difficult to interpret but should not be considered a definitive diagnostic test in the absence of an independent reference standard.

title: Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: Technical Advances, Clinical Applications, and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Radiotherapy is an essential treatment modality for cervical cancer and has evolved substantially with advances in image guidance and treatment delivery. This review summarizes recent technological developments in external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy, their clinical applications, and future directions, with particular consideration of Japanese practice in an international context. In external beam radiotherapy, conventional techniques incorporating central shielding are increasingly being replaced by intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) and volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT). Daily three-dimensional image-guided radiotherapy (3D-IGRT) is essential for the safe implementation of these techniques because of substantial uterine motion and deformation. In brachytherapy, the transition from two-dimensional point-based prescription to three-dimensional image-guided treatment has enabled individualized assessment of target coverage and doses to organs at risk. Although magnetic resonance imaging-based brachytherapy is internationally recommended, computed tomography-based planning predominates in Japan and has achieved favorable outcomes, despite some studies reporting lower cumulative target doses than those recommended internationally. Intracavitary/interstitial brachytherapy (IC/IS BT) further improves dose distribution by combining intracavitary applicators with interstitial needles, particularly when adequate target coverage cannot be achieved with standard intracavitary brachytherapy alone. Future advances may include artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted treatment planning and adaptive workflows, tissue spacers to overcome anatomical constraints, and the incorporation of genomic, multi-omics, and radiomics information. Integrating these approaches may enable cervical cancer radiotherapy to progress beyond increasingly safe and precise treatment toward personalized care tailored to individual patient and tumor characteristics.

title: Hidden in Plain Sight: A Case Report of a Rare Subserous Uterine Adenomyoma Mimicking an Ovarian Cyst With Literature Review.
abstract: The uterine corpus adenomyoma is a benign mixed epithelial and mesenchymal tumor, classified by the World Health Organization, fifth edition (2020), as a distinct lesion composed of endometrioid-type glands, endometrioid-type stroma, and smooth muscle. Subserosal adenomyomas with a pedunculated polypoid configuration represent a rare morphological presentation. We describe the case of a 46-year-old woman who presented for surgical evaluation of a right ovarian mass. Preoperative investigations, including transvaginal pelvic ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), showed a right adnexal cystic lesion. The patient underwent robot-assisted laparoscopy that suggested a subserosal cystic adenomyoma of the posterior uterine wall, a diagnosis confirmed by histological examination. This case underscores the importance of detailed intraoperative and pathological assessment for diagnosing pedunculated subserosal adenomyoma, which may be misdiagnosed clinically or radiologically. In similar situations, it is essential to consider the possibility of a subserosal adenomyoma to ensure appropriate preoperative counseling for the patient.

title: Hepatic Steatosis in People With Chronic Hepatitis B in Africa: Prevalence, Correlates, and Clinical Significance.
abstract: To address data gaps around metabolic liver disease in Africa, within the Hepatitis B in Africa Collaborative Network (HEPSANET), we evaluated participants with chronic hepatitis B virus infection (CHB) for steatotic liver disease (SLD) using transient elastography with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). Using multivariable logistic regression, we identified sociodemographic, anthropometric, and clinical associations with SLD (CAP ≥ 248 dB/m), and evaluated whether SLD severity was independently associated with fibrosis. Short-term impacts of SLD on mortality were also assessed with Cox proportional hazards analysis. We also evaluated the diagnostic performance of B-mode ultrasound for SLD, with CAP as reference. Across 6 countries and 1601 participants (age range, 12-80 years; 39.5% female; 4% with diabetes; 11% unhealthy alcohol use; median body mass index, 24.4), 421 (26.3%) had SLD; 219 (13.7%) had severe steatosis (CAP ≥ 280 dB/m). Older age, male sex, overweight and obesity, and HIV-negative status were associated with SLD. After adjusting for age, sex, HIV status, HBV treatment, and country, severe steatosis, but not mild and moderate forms (i.e., 248-279 dB/m), was associated with a 8.4% (95%, 1.9%-14.9%) increased probability of fibrosis. Over limited follow-up (median 2.69 years) and small number of deaths, SLD was not associated with all-cause or liver-related mortality. B-mode ultrasound had low sensitivity for SLD, overall or when severe, but specificity was 95%. In conclusion, SLD was common in people with CHB in Africa and its severe form was associated with liver fibrosis. These data support screening for metabolic comorbidities as part of HBV care and treatment in Africa.

title: Application of Combined Gastric Tube Tip Manometry and Auscultation for Nasogastric Tube Positioning in Neurocritical Care Patients With Artificial Airways: A Prospective Diagnostic Pilot Study.
abstract: Background Nasogastric tube placement is central to enteral nutrition support in neurocritical care patients. However, tube malposition, particularly accidental placement into the airway, can lead to fatal complications. Aim To assess the accuracy of a combined gastric tube tip manometry and auscultation approach for confirming nasogastric tube placement in neurocritical care patients with artificial airways. Study design This prospective study enrolled patients who underwent nasogastric tube insertion in the neurocritical care unit of a tertiary hospital in China between January 2025 and May 2025. Using chest X-ray as the reference standard, we compared the sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), positive likelihood ratio (PLR) and negative likelihood ratio (NLR) for gastric tube tip manometry alone, auscultation alone and their combination. Results In total, 120 patients participated. X-ray confirmed correct nasogastric tube positioning in 119 patients and malposition in 1 patient. For gastric tube tip manometry alone, the sensitivity was 97.48%, with a specificity of 0%, a positive predictive value (PPV) of 99.15% and a negative predictive value (NPV) of 0%. Auscultation alone yielded a sensitivity of 90.76%, a specificity of 100%, a PPV of 100% and an NPV of 8.33%. The combined manometry-plus-auscultation approach had a sensitivity of 88.24%, a specificity of 100%, a PPV of 100% and an NPV of 6.67%. Conclusions The combined gastric tube tip manometry and auscultation method might serve as an adjunctive bedside strategy for confirming nasogastric tube placement in neurocritical care patients with artificial airways. However, only one malpositioned tube was observed in this study; the specificity and NPV should be interpreted with caution. Relevance to clinical practice When gastric aspirate cannot be obtained or immediate chest radiography is impractical, combined gastric tube tip manometry and auscultation provide a feasible, radiation-free bedside pathway for confirming nasogastric tube position; equivocal or negative bedside findings should still be verified radiographically before feeding. Trial registration The study was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2300078001).

title: Machine Learning Prediction of Orthodontic Extraction Patterns Using Multimodal Features Derived From Intraoral Scans and Lateral Cephalometric Radiographs.
abstract: Objective To develop and evaluate a machine learning framework for predicting orthodontic extraction patterns using features extracted from pretreatment intraoral scans (IOS) and lateral cephalometric radiographs (LCRs). Materials and methods This retrospective study included 420 subjects (mean age, 17.1 years; 61% female) with treatment plans involving dental extractions. Expert consensus-derived reference labels were established using a validated Delphi process involving four orthodontic experts. The dataset was randomly split into two mutually exclusive subsets: 30% for hyperparameter optimization using grid search with five-fold cross-validation and 70% (n = 294) for model development and evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV). Performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, likelihood ratios and F1 score. Results The Gradient Boosting classifier trained exclusively on canine-molar relationship features achieved the highest overall classification accuracy (79.9%), whereas the Random Forest multimodal model incorporating all IOS- and LCR-derived features achieved 78.2% accuracy and did not provide a significant improvement over canine-molar relationship features alone. SHAP analysis identified canine and molar relationships as the most influential predictors. For the Random Forest multimodal model, class-specific sensitivity (recall) was 84% for Class I, 77% for Class II, and 48% for Class III. Conclusions Sagittal canine-molar relationship features contained the greatest discriminative information for extraction pattern classification in this dataset, and incorporating the full multimodal feature set did not improve predictive performance. The substantially lower sensitivity for the underrepresented Class III pattern highlights the need for larger, more balanced datasets.

title: Balancing Iliac Crest Avoidance and Neural Safety in L5/S1 TELD: Quantitative Identification of a Candidate Balanced Trajectory Window Using AI-Assisted 3D MRI Reconstruction.
abstract: Objective Transforaminal endoscopic lumbar discectomy (TELD) at L5/S1 is challenging due to the iliac crest barrier. Conventional planning relies on CT or 2D imaging, inherently lacking soft-tissue contrast to visualize neural structures. title: Association of Subscapularis Tear Severity With Posterosuperior Cuff Tear Morphology in a Combined-Tear Surgical Cohort: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Objectives In combined tears, the relationship between posterosuperior cuff tear (PSCT) morphology and subscapularis (SSC) tear severity is unknown. This study aimed to determine whether PSCT morphology is associated with SSC tear severity, which morphologies are associated with complete SSC rupture, and whether any association is confined to a particular severity threshold and persists after accounting for classification uncertainty and overall cuff extent. Methods A retrospective review of 368 patients who underwent arthroscopic surgery for combined, chronic, full-thickness PSCTs with concomitant SSC tears between 2016 and 2023 was conducted. High-resolution preoperative MRI and high-definition intraoperative video recordings were used to classify PSCT morphology (crescent, U-shaped, anterior L-shaped, posterior L-shaped, massive-retracted) and SSC tears (Lafosse Types I-V). Interobserver agreement was almost perfect for both classifications. Binary logistic regression (adjusted for age, sex, side, and BMI) was used to evaluate associations with complete subscapularis rupture (Lafosse IV/V). Results The mean patient age was 60.3 ± 9.2 years. PSCT morphology was significantly associated with SSC tear severity (Monte Carlo P less than 0.001; Cramer's V 0.234). The proportion with complete SSC rupture rose from 23.8% in posterior L-shaped and 25.6% in crescent tears to 39.6% in U-shaped, 60.9% in anterior L-shaped, and 71.4% in massive-retracted tears. Complete subscapularis rupture was significantly more likely in anterior L-shaped (adjusted OR 4.50, 95% CI 1.86 to 11.41) and massive-retracted morphologies (adjusted OR 7.12, 95% CI 2.24 to 27.17), both surviving correction (adjusted p = 0.003). Posterior L-shaped and U-shaped morphologies showed no significant difference from crescent tears. Conclusion In surgically treated combined tears, PSCT morphology shows a graded association with SSC tear severity that is concentrated in the anterior L-shaped and massive-retracted morphology patterns. However, because most complete ruptures overall occurred within crescent tears due to their high prevalence, morphology alone cannot serve as a definitive diagnostic rule-out tool. Nevertheless, anterior L-shaped or massive-retracted PSCT patterns warrant systematic inspection of the SSC.

title: The Clinical Outcome of a Fluoroscopy-Free "4-Step Cam Resection" Technique Compared With the Traditional Technique for Arthroscopic Treatment of Cam-Type Femoroacetabular Impingement.
abstract: Purpose To compare the clinical outcomes of the novel fluoroscopy-free "4-step cam resection" technique with the traditional cam resection method for treating cam-type FAI during hip arthroscopy. No established consensus exists on a standardized, reproducible technique that ensures complete cam resection without intraoperative fluoroscopy, and residual anterolateral cam deformity remains a leading cause of persistent impingement and revision surgery. The present study was therefore performed to determine whether the 4-step technique improves the completeness of cam resection compared with the conventional single-position technique. Methods Patients with symptomatic femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) who underwent the "4-step cam resection" technique between January 2021 and January 2022 were included. The 4-step intervention consisted of femoral head-neck osteoplasty performed sequentially with the hip placed in four positions: (i) 10° of flexion in maximal internal rotation; (ii) 10° of flexion in neutral rotation; (iii) 30° of flexion with rotation from internal to external; and (iv) 45° of flexion with rotation from internal to external. In the traditional technique, the cam lesion was resected with the hip in a single position of approximately 45° of flexion. No intraoperative fluoroscopy was used in either group. A historical control group extracted from our database was matched in a 1:1 ratio based on demographic and preoperative clinical variables. Outcomes were assessed using the Harris Hip Score (HHS), Hip Outcome Score (HOS), and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain. Radiographic measurements, including the lateral center-edge angle (LCEA) and alpha angle and gamma angle, were evaluated pre- and postoperatively. Results A total of 36 patients (36/40, 90.0%) in the study group (Group A, "4-step cam resection" technique) completed the final follow-up and 36 patients were matched as the control group (Group B, traditional technique). At a mean follow-up of 29 months, both groups demonstrated significant improvements in HOS, HHS, and VAS scores postoperatively (p < 0.05). Radiographic parameters including alpha angle, gamma angle, and LCEA were significantly reduced compared to preoperative values, with Group A showing significantly lower gamma angles and VAS for pain and a higher HOS-Sports score compared to Group B. The correlation analysis revealed that VAS (correlation coefficient = 0.281, p = 0.017) was correlated with gamma angle at the final follow-up. Conclusion The "4-step cam resection" technique achieves comparable subjective outcomes compared with the traditional technique and is associated with a greater decrease of gamma angle, lower VAS score, and better HOS-Sports outcome.

title: Application of Extraperitoneal Laparo-Endoscopic Single-Site Surgery in the Treatment of Lumbosacral Trunk Entrapment: A Cadaveric Study and Clinical Case Series.
abstract: Objective Management of pelvic fracture with lumbosacral trunk entrapment remains controversial. Open surgery (OS) carries significant technical challenges and risks. Our team innovatively proposed extraperitoneal laparo-endoscopic single-site surgery (ELESS) to explore and release the lumbosacral trunk. This study aimed to identify the key anatomical parameters of the lumbosacral trunk, to introduce ELESS techniques for exploration and release of lumbosacral trunk entrapment, and to evaluate its safety, feasibility, and clinical efficacy compared to OS. Methods This study measured lumbosacral trunk parameters in 12 cadavers, and retrospectively analyzed clinical data of 36 patients with lumbosacral trunk entrapment from May 2022 to September 2024. Combined with anatomical data, preoperative enhanced CT and MRN tests, the lumbosacral trunk decompression surgery was performed precisely via ELESS (n = 16) and OS (n = 20). Demographic, surgical technique details, and clinical outcomes were obtained from patient records. Independent samples t-tests, Mann-Whitney U test, or the Chi-square test were used to perform comparisons. Results The distance from the start of lumbosacral trunk to the sacroiliac joint was 14.85 ± 1.43 mm. The total length of the lumbosacral trunk was 34.95 ± 2.13 mm, and its width was 7.92 ± 1.11 mm. The patients were followed up for at least 16 months. The ELESS group demonstrated a significantly shorter operative time (131.5 ± 13.6 min) and reduced intraoperative blood loss (119.1 ± 28.1 mL) compared to the OS group (151.7 ± 27.9 min and 1010.5 ± 118.6 mL, p < 0.05). The incision visual analogue scale (VAS) scores in the ELESS group were lower than the OS group (p < 0.05). The muscle strength recovery rate was 88% in the ELESS group, showing no significant difference from the OS group (85%, p = 0.832). Sensory function recovery was observed in all patients. Conclusions Anatomical data is essential to identify and locate the lumbosacral trunk during surgery. The ELESS for lumbosacral trunk decompression offers the advantages of precision, minimal invasiveness, and safety. Compared to traditional OS, the ELESS is associated with less bleeding and shorter operative time, representing a reliable option for managing pelvic fractures with lumbosacral trunk entrapment.

title: Concurrent Long Thoracic and Lateral Cutaneous Intercostal Nerve Entrapment After Chest Tube Thoracostomy Causing Scapular Winging and Chest Wall Pain: Diagnosis With Ultrasound and Treatment With Hydrodissection.
abstract: Background Chest tube thoracostomy may cause iatrogenic nerve injury, resulting in persistent pain and functional impairment. Long thoracic nerve (LTN) palsy after chest tube placement has been described, but concurrent involvement of the LTN and the lateral cutaneous branch of an intercostal nerve (LCIN) appears to be rarely reported. We describe a patient with persistent post-thoracostomy chest wall pain and scapular winging in whom musculoskeletal ultrasonography identified entrapment of both nerves. Case presentation A 43-year-old man presented with severe left shoulder and chest wall pain 6 months after chest tube placement for traumatic hemopneumothorax. Examination demonstrated focal tenderness, dysesthesia, and mechanical allodynia at the chest tube scar, along with medial/inferior scapular winging during serratus anterior provocative testing. Shoulder range of motion was full on examination; however, forward flexion beyond 15° markedly aggravated pain, resulting in pain-related reluctance to move the shoulder. Manual muscle testing was 4+/5 before treatment because pain limited force generation. Musculoskeletal ultrasound demonstrated focal abnormality of the LTN where it pierced the axillary fascia over the sixth rib, with loss of fascicular definition and reduced glide, and tethering/thickening of the LCIN within scar tissue at the prior tube insertion site. Symptom reproduction with sonopalpation supported the clinical relevance of both findings. Intervention and results Ultrasound-guided hydrodissection using 5% dextrose in water was performed around both nerves. A total of approximately 40 mL of 5% dextrose in water was used, with 20 mL administered per nerve. Immediately after the first procedure, pain improved from NRS 9/10 to 2/10, with marked reduction in pain during shoulder movement, including forward flexion. The patient subsequently underwent 5 treatment sessions at 2-week intervals over 10 weeks. During follow-up, manual muscle testing improved to 5/5 without pain, scapular winging was no longer evident on provocative testing, and the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index improved from pain/disability scores of 25/15 to 6/4. At the sixth follow-up visit, pain and function were satisfactory, and the patient elected continued monitoring without further intervention. At 1-year follow-up, treatment efficacy remained sustained without recurrence. Conclusion In patients with persistent shoulder or chest wall pain after chest tube thoracostomy, iatrogenic peripheral nerve entrapment should be considered. This case highlights the value of a focused neuromuscular examination and musculoskeletal ultrasound for identifying concurrent motor and sensory nerve involvement and suggests that ultrasound-guided hydrodissection may be a useful minimally invasive treatment. Because electrodiagnostic studies were not performed, the findings are most consistent with entrapment/neurapraxia with dynamic tethering rather than electrodiagnostically proven axonal palsy.

Because electrodiagnostic studies were not performed, the findings are most consistent with entrapment/neurapraxia with dynamic tethering rather than electrodiagnostically proven axonal palsy.

title: Detection of Urinary Round Cells in a Dog With IgA Paraproteinemia: A Case of Myeloma-Related Disorder.
abstract: An 11-year-old neutered male Rottweiler mixed-breed dog was presented with apathy, anorexia, and polyuria/polydipsia. Clinicopathologic evaluation revealed hypercalcemia, azotemia, mild hyperproteinemia, and hyperglobulinemia, and proteinuria with concurrent glucosuria. Urinary cytology identified numerous neoplastic round cells morphologically consistent with plasma cells. Abdominal ultrasound demonstrated hepatic and splenic hypoechoic lesions, lymphadenomegaly, and hypoechoic prostatic parenchyma. Cytology of aspirates from hepatic and splenic lesions revealed the same neoplastic round cell population as observed in the urine. Based on these findings, a presumptive diagnosis of myeloma-related disorder (MRD), most likely multiple myeloma (MM), was made. Further laboratory investigations were pursued with serum protein electrophoresis (SPE) and immunofixation (IM), as well as immunocytochemistry. SPE coupled with IM revealed an IgA paraproteinemia, and immunocytochemistry findings were suggestive of plasma cell differentiation. The present findings are indicative of an MRD. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first description of plasmacytoid cells in urine from a dog with concurrent paraproteinemia, highlighting urine cytology as a potential non-invasive diagnostic tool for MRD.

title: Meibomian Gland Epithelioma Mimicking Eyelid Squamous Cell Carcinoma in a Hereford-Cross Steer.
abstract: Objective To describe the clinical presentation and histopathology of a meibomian gland epithelioma that clinically resembled squamous cell carcinoma in a steer. Animal studied A 15 year-old Hereford-Lowline cross steer presented for evaluation of an approximately 2 × 4 cm ulcerated, pedunculated eyelid mass arising from the right inferior eyelid margin. Procedures Excision of the mass followed by adjunctive cryotherapy was performed. The mass was submitted for histopathologic analysis. Results Histopathologic evaluation revealed the mass to be consistent with a meibomian gland epithelioma, a neoplastic proliferation of the basal/reserve cells of the meibomian gland. The steer recovered routinely from the procedure with no evidence of regrowth of the mass at 13 months post-operatively. Conclusion Meibomian gland epitheliomas are one of the most common eyelid tumors of dogs; however, this is the first known report of a histologically confirmed meibomian gland epithelioma in cattle. Clinically, the mass resembled the appearance of squamous cell carcinoma, a common eyelid tumor in Hereford cattle. The clinical misclassification of a benign eyelid mass as squamous cell carcinoma could lead to unnecessary aggressive management such as enucleation, exenteration, or culling. This case confirms the importance of histopathologic analysis of excised tissues to reach an accurate diagnosis and appropriate treatment and follow-up plans.

title: Idiopathic Granulomatous Inflammation of the Periocular Structures in Four Dogs: Clinical, Histopathological, and Imaging Findings and Therapeutic Outcome.
abstract: Purpose To describe cases of canine idiopathic periocular granulomatous inflammation. Material and methods Clinical records were reviewed. Animal studied At the time of presentation, the four patients (German Shepherd dog, mixed breed, Magyar Vizsla, Hovawart) were 1.5-5 (mean 3.75) years old. All dogs were female; two were spayed. Lesions were unilateral in 3/4 cases. Dogs presented with ulcerated (1) or non-ulcerated (3) mass lesions affecting the periocular skin (3/4), medial canthal area (2/4), or third eyelid (1/4). Results Incisional biopsies revealed pyogranulomatous inflammation in three and granulomatous inflammation in one case. There was no evidence of microbial infection in the specimens. Patients received anti-inflammatory or immunosuppressive dosages of systemic corticosteroids. Three dogs also received systemic cyclosporin (5 mg/kg, sid), and one dog received topical cyclosporin (0.1%, bid). One dog underwent surgical debulking of a circumscribed mass within the left lower eyelid prior to immunosuppressive therapy and developed an additional swelling on the left upper eyelid. Remission of clinical signs was achieved in all patients. Dogs were treated for 5 to 11 months (mean 8.7). No recurrence was reported in 4/4 patients during a mean follow-up period of 17.3 months. In 3/4patients, there was no recurrence within an average of 11 months after discontinuation of therapy. One dog was lost to follow-up. Conclusion Idiopathic granulomatous inflammation is a differential diagnosis for periocular mass lesions. Its diagnosis is based on histopathology and the exclusion of other causes of granulomatous inflammation.

title: Computed Tomographic Findings of Hepatic Rupture Associated With Amyloidosis in a Young Siamese Cat.
abstract: A 3-year-old neutered male Siamese cat with chronic anorexia showed anemia and elevated liver enzyme levels. Ultrasonography disclosed multiple diffusely heterogeneous hepatic lesions and peritoneal effusion, which was identified as hemoabdomen upon fluid analysis. Computed tomography showed finger-like hypoattenuation extending from the left hepatic margin with focal margin loss in the delayed phase, suggesting hepatic rupture. Infiltrative hepatic diseases were considered, and amyloidosis was the top differential diagnosis given the patient's young age, breed predisposition, and suspected hepatic rupture. Blood oozing was confirmed via laparotomy, and Congo red staining established hepatic amyloidosis, though amyloid typing was not pursued.

title: Radiographic Comparison of Pulmonary Lobar Vasculature Dimensions in Medically Managed and Drug-Naive Dogs With Left Heart Failure Secondary to Myxomatous Mitral Valve Disease.
abstract: Myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) is the most common acquired cause of left heart failure (LHF) in dogs, and radiographic identification of pulmonary venous enlargement is traditionally used to support the diagnosis of LHF. However, the absence of venous enlargement has been anecdotally observed after initiation of therapy. Therefore, we aimed to compare radiographic pulmonary vessel size in LHF patients with ongoing medical management ± receiving acute rescue therapy. Dogs with echocardiographically confirmed MMVD and radiographic cardiogenic pulmonary edema were retrospectively selected. Pulmonary lobar artery and vein widths were measured using standardized rib-to-vessel ratios: cranial vessels at the intersection with the fourth rib on lateral projections and caudal vessels at the ninth rib on ventrodorsal/dorsoventral projections. Pulmonary vein-to-artery (PV/PA) and vessel-to-rib ratios were calculated, with enlargement defined as >1.2 and small vessel size as <0.8, and treatment groups were compared using Welch-corrected t-tests. 200 radiographic studies from 163 dogs were reviewed. In all dogs, the veins measured larger than the arteries in all lung lobes. Chronically untreated dogs who received furosemide immediately before radiographs had no venous enlargement. All other groups had vascular asymmetry or venous enlargement in at least two lung lobes. All control dogs with reoccurrence of LHF had absence of venous enlargement after initiation of therapy. Pulmonary venous enlargement was most pronounced in the right caudal lung lobe. These findings indicate that dogs chronically managed for MMVD may decompensate into LHF without radiographic pulmonary venous enlargement and that furosemide administration prior to imaging can normalize vessel size.

title: Computed Tomographic Findings of Ischemic Necrosis of the Accessory Carpal Bone in a Dog.
abstract: A 1-year-and-9-month-old Golden Retriever presented with a 9-month history of right thoracic limb lameness. Radiographs revealed a monostotic, expansile lesion of the right accessory carpal bone (ACB). A computed tomography (CT) confirmed the aggressive nature of the lesion, demonstrating multifocal moth-eaten osteolysis, sclerosis, periosteal reaction, and flexor carpi ulnaris tendinopathy. Differential diagnoses included the ischemic necrosis of the ACB, osteomyelitis, and primary bone neoplasia. Histopathology confirmed osteonecrosis. This case highlights the value of CT in evaluating aggressive carpal lesions and identifies ischemic necrosis as an important differential diagnosis. This case represents the first CT description of this disease in dogs.

title: Evaluation of Intracranial Lesions Using Deep Learning-Based Reconstruction in Canine Brain MRI: Comparison With Conventional Reconstruction on T2-Weighted and FLAIR Sequences.
abstract: Obtaining high-resolution brain MRI in small animals is challenging due to the inherent trade-off between image quality and acquisition time. Deep learning-based reconstruction (DLR) has emerged as a solution to improve image quality without prolonging scan time; however, its clinical utility and potential risks, such as pseudolesions, remain insufficiently evaluated in veterinary patients. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of DLR on lesion assessment and image quality in canine brain MRI and to investigate potential limitations associated with its application. This retrospective study compared DLR with conventional reconstruction in 25 canine brain MRI examinations diagnosed with intracranial diseases. Transverse T2-weighted and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery sequences were reconstructed using both conventional and DLR methods. Quantitative analysis included signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and lesion edge sharpness. Two blinded radiologists assessed image quality, lesion conspicuity, artifacts, pseudolesions, and lesion masking. DLR images exhibited significantly higher SNR, CNR, and lesion edge sharpness than conventional images in both sequences (p < 0.05). DLR images also yielded significantly higher qualitative scores for image quality and lesion conspicuity (p < 0.05). Truncation artifact was significantly reduced, whereas motion and pulsation artifacts showed no improvement. No instances of pseudolesions or lesion masking were noted. DLR significantly improves image quality and lesion conspicuity in canine brain MRI and reduces truncation artifacts; however, it does not mitigate motion or pulsation interference. Collectively, these findings suggest that DLR has potential value for improving image quality and lesion visibility in canine brain MRI, whereas further studies are needed to determine its impact on diagnostic performance.

title: Accuracy of intraoperative gross margin assessment by veterinary surgeons compared with histologic margin evaluation: A multicenter prospective cohort study.
abstract: Objective To identify the sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and accuracy of intraoperative surgeon-perceived margin status via gross examination compared to histologic evaluation for marginal and wide cutaneous mass excisions. Study design Multicenter prospective cohort study. Animal population A total of 84 dogs and six cats with 102 cutaneous masses. Methods Four surgeons completed a survey assessing margin completeness after mass removal prior to histologic results. Results Surgeon ability to identify incomplete margins had a sensitivity of 56.3%, specificity of 87.2%, PPV of 45%, NPV of 91.5%, and accuracy of 82.4%. Surgeon margin assessment was correct in 58.5% of marginally excised and 98.4% of widely excised masses: odds ratio (OR) 0.024 (confidence interval [CI]: 0.003, 0.19). Margin assessment based upon cytologic malignancy status was correct in nine of 14 (64.3%) benign lesions and 75 of 88 (85.2%) malignant lesions: OR 0.31 (CI: 0.09, 1.1). Conclusion Surgeons did not have improved accuracy in margin assessment for cytologically benign masses compared with malignant masses. Surgeon margin assessment correctness may be influenced by surgical dose. Additionally, when surgeons suspected a complete margin, there was a high probability that the histologic margin was complete. Limitations included the diversity of cases enrolled, few participating surgeons, potential non-blinded assessment bias, and lack of clinical follow up. Clinical significance Veterinary surgeons can provide owners an assessment of margin completeness with a degree of confidence for wide mass excision. Caution should persist in assessment of marginally excised tumors. This information allows owners to contemplate further treatment pending histopathology results.

title: Intrametatarsal pad injection of indocyanine green for near-infrared fluorescence imaging of the thoracic duct in four dogs and two cats with chylothorax.
abstract: To assess the efficacy of direct near-infrared fluorescence (NIRF) using indocyanine green (ICG) via intrametatarsal pad injection in dogs and cats with idiopathic chylothorax. Retrospective case series of client-owned animals undergoing intrametatarsal ICG injection and thoracoscopic thoracic duct ligation between 2020 and 2025. A total of four dogs and two cats. Inclusion criteria consisted of cytologically confirmed chylothorax, preoperative computed tomography (CT) lymphangiogram (CTL), and known intraoperative injection of ICG in the metatarsal pad(s). Data collected included signalment, weight, preoperative diagnostics, number of ducts visualized intraoperatively, dose of ICG, additional doses required, and concordance with CTL. Time to visualization of the ICG in the thoracic duct, surgical procedures performed, and any intraoperative complications encountered were also reported. Postoperative data included time to discharge, time to first recheck, presence of fluid at first recheck, postoperative complications, status at last recheck, and total follow-up time. Median number of ducts seen between T10 and 13 region on preoperative CT was 2.5 (range: 1-4). The ICG dose ranged from 0.06 to 0.25 mg/kg, and two cases required additional injections to visualize the duct and all branches. A duct not previously seen on CT was visualized with NIRF in one dog. Median time to TD visualization was 7 min (range: 5-22 min). No intra- or postoperative complications due to the metatarsal injections were reported, and all patients were discharged. A total of 5/6 patients did not require thoracocentesis and were clinically well at a median last follow-up of 647 days (range: 454-793). Intrametatarsal injection of ICG appears effective for identification of the thoracic duct in animals with chylothorax.

title: Noise2Flow: single-image conditional mean denoising flows from weak-anchor couplings.
abstract: Purpose Single-image denoising is needed when clean targets and repeated acquisitions are unavailable, as in low-dose computed tomography (CT) and fluorescence microscopy. Existing per-image methods often assume pixel-wise noise independence, which fails under spatially correlated noise, and imperfect single-image denoisers commonly leave residual noise. We learn a proxy mean-velocity direction field from one noisy image so that a single transport step exceeds the imperfect anchors used as supervision. Approach Noise2Flow runs weak single-image denoisers on the noisy image to form source-target couplings. The displacement from input to anchor is a directional proxy for the mean restoration velocity. For each imposed linear segment, MeanFlow's finite-interval average velocity reduces exactly to a constant secant. A flow network is trained with a direction-normalized objective that regularizes predictions at states in a stochastic tube around the noisy-to-anchor segment toward a common secant direction. At inference, the weak denoisers are discarded; one update with a calibrated transport budget restores the image. originalAbstract:
Purpose

Single-image denoising is needed when clean targets and repeated acquisitions are unavailable, as in low-dose computed tomography (CT) and fluorescence microscopy. Existing per-image methods often assume pixel-wise noise independence, which fails under spatially correlated noise, and imperfect single-image denoisers commonly leave residual noise. We learn a proxy mean-velocity direction field from one noisy image so that a single transport step exceeds the imperfect anchors used as supervision.

Approach

Noise2Flow runs weak single-image denoisers on the noisy image to form source-target couplings. The displacement from input to anchor is a directional proxy for the mean restoration velocity. For each imposed linear segment, MeanFlow's finite-interval average velocity reduces exactly to a constant secant. A flow network is trained with a direction-normalized objective that regularizes predictions at states in a stochastic tube around the noisy-to-anchor segment toward a common secant direction. At inference, the weak denoisers are discarded; one update with a calibrated transport budget restores the image.

Results

On the fluorescence microscopy denoising (FMD) test set of 48 images, Noise2Flow reaches 34.91 dB peak signal-to-noise ratio and 0.887 structural similarity, 0.52 dB above Filter2Noise, and 1.00 dB above Noise2Detail. On 1311 low-dose CT slices from 10 Mayo Clinic patients, it reaches 28.82 dB and 0.714, 0.91 dB above Filter2Noise and 1.23 dB above Noise2Detail. One-step inference is within 0.11 dB of 10-step Heun; tube sampling improves the 10-step Heun result relative to on-segment training; a calibrated extrapolation factor moves the flow past residual-noise anchors of varying quality.

Conclusions

A proxy mean-velocity direction field can be learned from a single noisy medical image by treating weak-denoiser outputs as directional anchors rather than final targets. The straight proxy path defines the one-step endpoint update; tube regularization and calibrated extrapolation carry that update past residual-noise anchors. The learned flow exceeds residual-noise anchors and supports reference-free restoration in data-limited imaging.

title: Representation geometry and task performance in vision-language modeling for computed tomography enterography.
abstract: Purpose Computed tomography (CT) enterography is central to inflammatory bowel disease evaluation, but optimal representation choices for vision-language learning on this volumetric modality are unclear. We establish baseline performance and quantify how aggregation, slice encoding, and retrieval context affect classification, retrieval, and report generation. Approach We fine-tuned vision-language models on abdominal CT enterography with parameter-efficient adapters and compared (i) mean versus attention pooling of slice embeddings, (ii) multiwindow red-green-blue Hounsfield-unit encoding versus multiplanar sampling for added spatial coverage, and (iii) report generation with versus without retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). A three-teacher pseudolabel framework enabled evaluation without expert annotations. Classification and retrieval comparisons used three training seeds. Results Mean and attention pooling achieved the same mean three-class disease classification accuracy (55.7%; standard deviations of 2.0 and 2.4 percentage points) at the largest low-rank adaptation capacity. Neither consistently outperformed the other at matched capacity with central sampling. Sixteen slices at 20% to 80% had higher classification accuracy than 8 slices, 32 slices, and 10% to 90% sampling in all three seeds for both pooling methods. The tested multiplanar configurations had lower classification accuracy. For report generation, fine-tuning without retrieval performed at prevalence-matched chance for within-1 report-label agreement (70.4% versus 71.0% random). RAG improved within-1 report-label agreement by 7 to 14 points over chance and reduced ordinal mean absolute error from 0.98 to 0.80-0.89. Conclusions Slice sampling and tissue-contrast-focused encoding affect performance in CT enterography vision-language systems, and RAG improved report-label agreement over the fine-tuned baseline. These results provide initial baselines and practical guidance for multimodal learning in volumetric CT.

title: Evaluating GPT-5 as a generalist multimodal clinical model.
abstract: Purpose The transition from task-specific artificial intelligence toward general-purpose foundation models raises fundamental questions about their capacity to support the integrated reasoning required in clinical medicine, where diagnosis demands synthesis of ambiguous patient narratives, laboratory data, and multimodal imaging. Approach We provide the first controlled, cross-sectional evaluation of the GPT-5 family (GPT-5, GPT-5 Mini, and GPT-5nano) against its predecessor GPT-4o across a diverse spectrum of clinically grounded tasks, grounded tasks, including the United States Medical Licensing Examination, text-based, text-based reasoning benchmarks (MedQA and MedXpertQA Text), and visual question answering (VQA) in neuroradiology (BraTS), digital pathology (PathVQA and BreakHis), and mammography (EMBED, InBreast, Chinese Mammography Database, and CBIS-DDSM) using a standardized zero-shot chain-of-thought protocol. Results GPT-5 demonstrated substantial performance gains with absolute improvements exceeding 25 percentage points on MedXpertQA. When tasked with multimodal synthesis, GPT-5 effectively leveraged its enhanced training corpora to achieve state-of-the-art or competitive performance across most VQA benchmarks and outperformed GPT-4o by margins of 10% to 40% in mammography tasks requiring fine-grained lesion characterization. However, performance remained moderate in neuroradiology (44% macro-average accuracy) and lagged substantially behind domain-specific models in mammography, where specialized systems exceed 80% accuracy compared with GPT-5's 52% to 64%. Conclusions These findings indicate that although GPT-5 represents a meaningful advance toward general, multimodal clinical inference, generalist models are still not yet substitutes for purpose-built systems in highly specialized, perception-critical tasks. We delineate the current VQA landscape, positioning GPT-5 as a powerful adjunct capable of holistic inference while underscoring that domain adaptation, rigorous validation, and guarantees of reasoning transparency remain essential prerequisites for clinical deployment.

title: Pathology-targeted PET/CT imaging of early lupus nephritis via a <sup>68</sup>Ga-labeled single-stranded DNA probe.
abstract: As a major cause of morbidity in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), the prognosis of lupus nephritis (LN) critically depends on early detection and timely intervention. However, current diagnostic approaches remain suboptimal: renal biopsy is invasive and unsuitable for longitudinal monitoring, while conventional urine tests lack sensitivity for early-stage disease. Here, we report a molecular imaging strategy designed to target the pathogenic DNA-anti-dsDNA antibody axis for non-invasive detection of LN. We engineered a gallium-68-labeled single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) probe ([ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-ssDNA) and evaluated its diagnostic performance and biosafety in the spontaneous MRL/lpr lupus mouse model. The probe showed disease-associated and sustained renal accumulation in 16-week-old diseased MRL/lpr mice, with progressively increasing kidney-to-background contrast. More importantly, [ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-ssDNA enabled detection of renal immune complex deposition as early as 10 weeks of age, preceding abnormalities in conventional renal function markers and positive findings in renal histology by approximately two weeks. Mechanistically, the ssDNA backbone demonstrated favorable biocompatibility, without exacerbating autoimmune phenotypes or inducing Toll-like receptor-mediated signaling pathways. In conclusion, this study establishes a robust proof-of-concept for pathology-targeted PET/CT imaging of immune complex deposition. By directly visualizing the disease-driving renal autoantibody deposition at the preclinical stage, prior to overt organ damage, this strategy shifts LN diagnosis to non-invasive, mechanism-based molecular visualization.

title: Human carotid plaque risk imaging using multiparametric photoacoustic and ultrasound fusion (hCAPRI).
abstract: Assessing the risk of carotid plaque rupture remains limited because current imaging methods cannot provide both plaque composition and structural information in real time. Here, we present human carotid plaque risk imaging (hCAPRI), a multiparametric photoacoustic and ultrasound (PA/US) fusion method for real-time carotid plaque assessment. hCAPRI combines PA imaging for detecting intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) with US imaging for evaluating the plaque structure. PA imaging measured IPH size and methemoglobin content, while US imaging assessed stenosis severity, calcification, and plaque thickness. Combining these PA/US parameters, we compute an hCAPRI score. In 171 carotid arteries (CAs) from 120 patients, hCAPRI revealed the relationships among the PA/US parameters. In 36 CAs validated with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), hCAPRI showed high agreement with MRI. The hCAPRI score achieved 89% sensitivity and 84% specificity for high-risk plaque classification. hCAPRI offers a low-cost, real-time, and contrast-free approach for carotid plaque risk imaging.

title: Lighting up necrotic neurons from traumatic brain injury with magnetic quantum dots to decode the cellular origin of MRI.
abstract: The diagnosis of traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains heavily constrained by the limitations of conventional imaging techniques in visualizing the pathological events that determine the disease progression and outcome. To address this clinical challenge, we report a manganese-doped near-infrared quantum dot (QD) to intrinsically integrate the highly sensitive optical imaging with clinical compatible magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Taking the advantages of optical imaging powered by whole-brain clearing and cellular resolution three-dimensional (3D) panoptic imaging, in combination with the systematic in vitro cell studies on different types of cells involved in TBI, we disclosed the interpretable pathology reflected by TBI imaging through the highly sensitive fluorescence of magnetic QDs, i.e., after systemic administration, the nanoprobes were extravasated through the compromised blood-brain barrier and then selectively phagocytosed by activated microglia, which subsequently migrated into the regions rich in dead neurons and neuronal debris. This microglia-mediated tropism decodes the signal origin of MRI enhanced by the nanometer-sized contrast agent, thereby transforming the MRI from an anatomical tool into a pathological reporter. A biocompatible Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticle of similar size was also compared with the magnetic QD mentioned above for validating the translational merits of nanoparticles in MRI diagnosis of TBI.

title: Characterization of herpes B virus isolated from wild cynomolgus macaques and its pathogenic effects in captive hosts.
abstract: Despite the high seroprevalence of herpes B virus (BV) among wild macaques, it remains unclear why BV is rarely transmitted to humans who live alongside macaques in their natural habitats. We investigated disease progression, host immune responses, viral shedding, histopathology, and immunohistochemistry of tissues after BV injection in cynomolgus macaques. BV was isolated from a wild Thai cynomolgus macaque living in southern Thailand and intramuscularly injected into four captive macaques (two males and two females) housed at the Animal Biosafety Level 3 facility. Over 49 days, all macaques remained clinically healthy but showed enlarged lymph nodes. IgM was detected on 9 days post-infection (dpi) and peaked at 13 dpi, while IgG appeared on 11 dpi and peaked at 28 dpi. No viral DNA was detected in oral, urogenital, or rectal swabs throughout the 49 day study period. However, viral DNA was identified in the spleen, sublingual gland, and trigeminal ganglia. Histopathology revealed tissue damage in the spleen and trigeminal ganglion, with BV immunoreactivity in the spleen. Overall, BV injection induces localized lymphoid and immune responses without causing clinical symptoms or viral shedding in natural macaque hosts. This may help explain why natural macaque hosts remain healthy and why human BV infections associated with wild cynomolgus macaques have rarely been documented.IMPORTANCEHerpes B virus (BV) isolated from a wild cynomolgus macaque was inoculated into captive macaques in an experimental setting. BV infection triggers localized lymphoid and immune responses (IgM and IgG) without causing clinical symptoms or viral shedding. Viral DNA was detected in the spleen, sublingual gland, and trigeminal ganglia. These insights improve our understanding of how BV interacts with its natural macaque hosts and shed light on the rare transmission of BV from wild macaques to humans.
