title: Phenotypic Variability in Individuals With Genotype-Matched EYS- and USH2A-Associated Autosomal-Recessive Retinitis Pigmentosa.
abstract: Purpose Variable expressivity is well recognized in autosomal-dominant inherited retinal diseases (IRDs) but is increasingly observed and less well defined in recessive IRDs. Despite the traditional view of recessive IRDs as monogenic disorders with high penetrance, phenotypic differences among individuals sharing identical biallelic variants suggest additional disease modifiers. We quantified genotype-phenotype concordance in EYS- and USH2A-associated retinitis pigmentosa (RP) and characterized phenotypic variability among individuals with identical primary genotypes. Methods Participants underwent standardized ophthalmic assessment with multimodal imaging. Longitudinal ellipsoid zone (EZ) widths were measured from optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans obtained ≥12 months apart. Baseline EZ width and age at OCT assessment were compared among individuals sharing identical primary genotypes. Genotype-matched comparisons in which younger individuals demonstrated smaller EZ widths than older counterparts were classified as age-discordant structural comparisons. Results Ninety patients (41 EYS, 49 USH2A) were included. Recurrent variants EYS c.6416G>A (p.Cys2139Tyr) and USH2A c.2802T>G (p.Cys934Trp) were identified in 46% and 35% of probands, respectively. Females showed greater baseline EZ preservation, although differences were not statistically significant. Marked variability was observed within matched genotypes. Several genotype-matched comparisons demonstrated age-discordant structural variability, including younger individuals with substantially smaller EZ widths than older genotype-matched counterparts. In EYS-associated disease, the largest discordant comparison demonstrated 85.4% less EZ preservation in the younger individuals despite younger age, and the corresponding value in USH2A-associated disease was 81.8%. Intrafamilial discordance further supported the possibility of modifying influences beyond the primary genotype. Conclusions Disease severity varied substantially among individuals sharing identical primary genotypes, supporting contributions from additional genetic or environmental modifiers. Translational relevance Recognition of variability within recessive IRDs has implications for prognosis, trial stratification, and interpretation of treatment response beyond genotype alone.
originalAbstract:
Purpose

Variable expressivity is well recognized in autosomal-dominant inherited retinal diseases (IRDs) but is increasingly observed and less well defined in recessive IRDs. Despite the traditional view of recessive IRDs as monogenic disorders with high penetrance, phenotypic differences among individuals sharing identical biallelic variants suggest additional disease modifiers. We quantified genotype-phenotype concordance in EYS- and USH2A-associated retinitis pigmentosa (RP) and characterized phenotypic variability among individuals with identical primary genotypes.

Methods

Participants underwent standardized ophthalmic assessment with multimodal imaging. Longitudinal ellipsoid zone (EZ) widths were measured from optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans obtained ≥12 months apart. Baseline EZ width and age at OCT assessment were compared among individuals sharing identical primary genotypes. Genotype-matched comparisons in which younger individuals demonstrated smaller EZ widths than older counterparts were classified as age-discordant structural comparisons.

Results

Ninety patients (41 EYS, 49 USH2A) were included. Recurrent variants EYS c.6416G>A (p.Cys2139Tyr) and USH2A c.2802T>G (p.Cys934Trp) were identified in 46% and 35% of probands, respectively. Females showed greater baseline EZ preservation, although differences were not statistically significant. Marked variability was observed within matched genotypes. Several genotype-matched comparisons demonstrated age-discordant structural variability, including younger individuals with substantially smaller EZ widths than older genotype-matched counterparts. In EYS-associated disease, the largest discordant comparison demonstrated 85.4% less EZ preservation in the younger individuals despite younger age, and the corresponding value in USH2A-associated disease was 81.8%. Intrafamilial discordance further supported the possibility of modifying influences beyond the primary genotype.

Conclusions

Disease severity varied substantially among individuals sharing identical primary genotypes, supporting contributions from additional genetic or environmental modifiers.

Translational relevance

Recognition of variability within recessive IRDs has implications for prognosis, trial stratification, and interpretation of treatment response beyond genotype alone.

title: Vascular Retinomics Decodes Panvascular Progression: A Retinal Polyvascular Disease Risk Index.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate whether color fundus photograph-derived vascular retinomics predicts progression from single vascular disease to polyvascular disease. Methods This prospective cohort study included UK Biobank participants with baseline single vascular disease and eligible color fundus photographs. Progression was defined as incident involvement of a previously unaffected coronary, cerebrovascular, or peripheral arterial bed. After LASSO-Cox and Boruta feature selection, eight survival-learning algorithms were compared. The best-performing model was refitted to derive the Retinal Polyvascular Disease Risk Index (RPVDRI). Performance was evaluated in the testing cohort and benchmarked against conventional clinical factors and SMART2. Results Among 2592 participants, 334 progressed during a median follow-up of 11.39 years. A 25-feature vascular retinomic panel was retained, and a gradient boosting machine performed best. In the testing cohort, the RPVDRI showed a graded association with progression after multivariable adjustment (highest vs. lowest tertile: hazard ratio, 1.97; 95% confidence interval, 1.03-3.74; P = 0.040; P for trend = 0.029). The RPVDRI achieved 3-, 5-, and 10-year areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.636, 0.716, and 0.628, respectively. Adding the RPVDRI to conventional clinical factors improved 5-year AUC by 0.113 (P = 0.002), whereas the corresponding improvement beyond SMART2 was 0.037 (P = 0.466). Shapley additive explanations linked predictions to multidomain features and co-attribution. Conclusions The RPVDRI was independently associated with polyvascular disease progression and may complement clinical risk assessment in secondary prevention, particularly in scalable or opportunistic settings where comprehensive clinical information is limited. Translational relevance Fundus-derived vascular retinomics may support precision secondary prevention by noninvasively stratifying residual polyvascular progression risk.

title: Static Perimetry-OCT Topographical Overlay Findings in the RUSH2A Study.
abstract: Purpose Ellipsoid zone (EZ) loss on optical coherence tomography (OCT) correlates with diminished sensitivity on static perimetry (SP). We explore a topographical overlay analysis in USH2A-related retinitis pigmentosa (RP) to develop novel endpoints of structural and functional change. Methods Subjects (N = 105) had SP (3× baseline; once annually for 4 years) and annual OCT. B-scans were segmented to outline the EZ. Overlays used visual field modeling and analysis (VFMA) software to superimpose the hill of vision (HOV) onto the en face infrared (IR) fundus image with EZ contours segmented from OCT volume scans. EZ border and three ribbons straddling the EZ border were ray cast onto the HOV. The HOV volume, HOV slope, mean sensitivity (MS), and peak sensitivity were measured. Mixed effect models were used to estimate change rates. Results Significant decrease over 4 years was found in all measures within the EZ, except slope and peak sensitivity. MS decreased for all ribbons, with outer ribbons showing greater progression than inner ribbons. Inner ribbons had larger decreases in volume and slope than outer ribbons. Conclusions SP-OCT overlay analysis showed faster loss of sensitivity outside the EZ margin. The widest ribbon outside the EZ showed greatest progression, suggesting more rapid vision loss occurring distal to the EZ margin. Slope progressed most within the widest inner ribbon, which could mean that slope change is a precursor to EZ loss. Translational relevance This research explores novel endpoints and concepts to characterize the disease progression in USH2A-related RP using imaging and functional overlay techniques.

title: Amblyopic Eyes Show Reduced Retinal Vessel Density Compared to Fellow Eyes Using Widefield Swept-Source Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography.
abstract: Purpose Amblyopia has traditionally been considered a purely functional disorder without an organic correlate. Recent optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) studies, however, revealed alterations in the central retinal vasculature of amblyopic eyes. This prospective, monocentric study is the first, to our knowledge, to employ widefield swept-source OCTA (WF-SS-OCTA) for a quantitative assessment of the retinal and choroidal vasculature extending to the periphery, comparing amblyopic eyes with healthy fellow eyes. Methods Patients with unilateral amblyopia were recruited at Münster University Hospital and underwent WF-SS-OCTA imaging. The superficial capillary plexus (SCP) and choroid were analyzed using AngioTool software. Results A total of 102 eyes from 51 patients were included. In amblyopic eyes, the SCP demonstrated significantly lower vessel pixel density (VPD) (P = 0.01), fewer junctions (P = 0.01), shorter vessel length (total and average, both P < 0.01), and increased lacunarity (P < 0.01) compared to fellow eyes, whereas the number of end points did not differ significantly (P = 0.10). Subgroup analysis showed that moderate amblyopia was associated with significantly lower VPD, fewer junctions, and shorter total vessel lengths compared to mild amblyopia, with no significant differences in end points or lacunarity. No significant differences were observed in choroidal vascular parameters (all P > 0.46). Conclusions These findings support an organic correlate of amblyopia, characterized by a less dense superficial retinal vascular network, possibly reflecting postnatal regression or impaired retinal vascular development due to inadequate visual stimulation in early childhood. Translational relevance WF-SS-OCTA may provide an objective imaging biomarker for amblyopia severity.

title: Cerebellar and frontal lobe alterations in pulmonary hypertension implicate an inflammatory lung vascular/brain axis.
abstract: Connections between vascular and neurocognitive diseases are emerging but remain poorly defined. Cognitive impairment is increasingly recognized in pulmonary hypertension (PH), a disease traditionally viewed as limited to the heart and lungs. Given that inflammation is shared by PH and neurodegenerative diseases, we investigated its role in driving brain and cognitive deficits in PH. Using structural and functional MRI data from UK Biobank (N = 248 PH) and a prospective validation cohort, we identified reduced cerebellar white matter volume, thinner frontal gyri, and weakened cerebellar-frontal connectivity in patients with PH but not in other heart or lung diseases. These changes were accompanied by worsened executive function and processing speed. Olink proteomics and targeted genomics linked inflammatory plasma proteins and a PH-associated nuclear receptor coactivator 7 (NCOA7) single nucleotide polymorphism, rs11154337, to these deficits. PH cerebellum showed increased microglial activation and white matter derangement. In PH mice, Ncoa7 deficiency worsened cerebellar inflammation and atrophy. Microglial functional assays, cerebellar single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic analyses further implicated Ncoa7-dependent lysosomal, inflammatory, and cell-specific mechanisms of cerebellar pathobiology. These findings identify NCOA7-linked inflammatory dysfunction in the cerebellar-frontal axis in PH, redefining this disease with neurologic consequences and thus offering neural targets for diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic development.

title: Quality, clinical utility, and economic implications of routine intraoperative cholangiography during laparoscopic cholecystectomy: A standardised audit study.
abstract: BackgroundLaparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) is the standard treatment for gallstone disease, but routine intraoperative cholangiography (IOC) remains controversial regarding image quality and downstream resource use. This audit evaluated routine IOC performance, quality, clinical utility, and financial impact.MethodsA retrospective audit assessed 279 consecutive adults undergoing LC with attempted IOC (January-December 2024). Image quality was assessed using a novel 12-point checklist applied independently by three trained readers, with consultant adjudication of disagreements. Outcomes included IOC success, image quality, clinical findings, subsequent interventions, and costs.ResultsBiliary cannulation succeeded in 93.2% (260 out of 279) of cases, but only 66.92% (174 out of 260) met the pre-specified high-quality threshold (≥6 of 8 core parameters). Visualisation was lowest for the cystic duct junction and right sectoral ducts. Sixteen significant findings were identified, including 11 choledocholithiasis cases. No bile duct injuries occurred. Equivocal IOC-driven imaging led to 14 postoperative magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatographies, of which only five demonstrated pathology. Low-yield downstream imaging and prolonged admissions generated £11,800 in excess costs.ConclusionsRoutine IOC is feasible, but variable technical quality drives unnecessary downstream investigations and healthcare expenditure. Standardised reporting using a 12-point checklist can improve quality and resource utilisation.

title: EXPRESS: Brain Age Gap from Non-Contrast CT Is Independently Associated with Functional Outcome after Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: BackgroundOutcomes after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) vary beyond lesion burden and clinical severity, suggesting a role for baseline structural brain vulnerability. We evaluated whether brain age gap (BrainAGE) derived from routine non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) is associated with functional outcome after AIS.MethodsWe analyzed 1,173 AIS patients from a prospective multicenter cohort. A deep learning model estimated brain age from contralesional baseline NCCT to minimize lesion-related confounding. BrainAGE was defined as predicted minus chronological age. The primary outcome was 90-day functional status, assessed using proportional odds regression adjusted for age, sex, baseline stroke severity, early ischemic changes, and reperfusion therapy.ResultsBrainAGE was higher in AIS patients than in controls (+3.1 ± 9.1 years; p<0.001). Higher BrainAGE was associated with worse functional outcome after adjustment for age, sex, and other clinical predictors (POR 1.091 per 5 years; 95% CI 1.023-1.162; p=0.008). BrainAGE improved model fit but modestly improved discrimination.ConclusionsBrainAGE from routine NCCT provided modest incremental prognostic information beyond age and conventional clinical predictors. These findings support CT-based BrainAGE as a marker of brain health complementary to established prognostic factors. Whether BrainAGE improves patient-level risk stratification or clinical decision-making requires independent external validation and prospective evaluation.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled medical image analysis in photon-counting CT: A review of segmentation, detection, classification and characterization, and automated quantification.
abstract: BackgroundPhoton-counting computed tomography (PCCT) provides finely sampled morphological images and energy-resolved products that may alter the behavior of artificial-intelligence models developed for conventional CT.ObjectiveThis review synthesizes downstream AI applications in PCCT and determines which study designs support claims of feasibility, transfer, spatial or spectral contribution, scanner advantage, and clinical utility.MethodsA structured narrative search identified original studies evaluating segmentation, detection, classification and characterization, and automated quantification on reconstructed PCCT images. Each analytical configuration was coded by task, effective input, model provenance, development or adaptation strategy, reference standard, comparator, testing independence, and evidence maturity.ResultsTechnical feasibility has been demonstrated across all four tasks. Established conventional-domain models often retained useful local performance on PCCT, while PCCT-native studies explored virtual monoenergetic images, threshold or energy-bin images, material maps, and multienergy feature spaces. However, small cohorts, repeated non-independent observations, incomplete external testing, limited matched PCCT-EID comparisons, and scarce spatial or spectral ablations restrict causal attribution. Prospective workflow evidence remains uncommon.ConclusionsPCCT creates important opportunities for AI-enabled image analysis, but availability of high-resolution or energy-resolved information does not establish its contribution to performance. Claims should be aligned with the comparator, ablation, reference standard, and validation design required to support them.

title: Brain Structural Changes in Blast-Exposed Special Operations Forces Soldiers.
abstract: Special Operations Forces (SOF) soldiers experience frequent low-level occupational blast exposure and mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), but the cumulative effects of these exposures on long-term neurological health remain poorly understood. The purpose of this longitudinal cohort study was to investigate associations between occupational blast exposure and brain structural change in SOF soldiers and to determine whether mTBI sustained between assessments moderated these associations. Male SOF soldiers ( n = 88) underwent T1- and T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging at two timepoints. Volumetric segmentation was performed using FreeSurfer. Main outcomes were percent change in global brain tissue volumes, including cerebral cortex, cerebral white matter, lateral ventricles, subcortical gray matter, and cerebellar cortex. Exposure was quantified as months between Time 1 and Time 2, used as a proxy for cumulative occupational blast exposure during time in a high-tempo operational unit. The number of self-reported mTBIs sustained between timepoints was categorized as 0, 1-2, or 3 or more injuries. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure was applied to control the false discovery rate. Greater occupational blast exposure predicted increased lateral ventricle percent change ( F 1,86 = 9.86; B = 0.126%; R 2 = 0.103; p = 0.002; p -adjusted = 0.012) and decreased cerebellar cortex percent change ( F 1,86 = 5.72; B = -0.074%; R 2 = 0.062; p = 0.019; p -adjusted = 0.047). Between-visit mTBI did not significantly moderate these associations. In this cohort of SOF soldiers, greater cumulative occupational blast exposure was associated with lateral ventricular expansion and cerebellar cortex volume loss. The rate of ventricular expansion observed in this study is atypical compared with expected change in healthy adults and may represent an early structural marker of blast-related brain vulnerability. Cerebellar cortex volume loss may reflect regional susceptibility to blast-related injury. Identifying brain structural changes associated with occupational blast exposure may help inform exposure-monitoring strategies and targeted interventions to preserve warfighter brain health and readiness.

title: The Association of MRI-Derived Tissue Bridge Morphometrics with Baseline Impairment and Recovery in Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury: A Subanalysis of the RISCIS Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Early prognostic biomarkers are essential to optimize treatment and trial design in spinal cord injury (SCI). The Riluzole in SCI Study (RISCIS), a multicenter randomized controlled trial, provided evidence on secondary analyses that riluzole improved functional recovery in acute cervical SCI. The current analysis uses magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to assess lesion and tissue bridge morphometrics against baseline impairment, functional recovery, and treatment response in RISCIS participants. In this preplanned ambispective subanalysis, 24 participants underwent T2-weighted MRI for acute cervical SCI together with neurological and functional assessments to 12 months. A subset also had diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), used to extract fractional anisotropy (FA) values. Segmentation with the Spinal Cord Toolbox (v7.2) gave ventral, dorsal, and total tissue-bridge widths and lesion volume and length. Associations with American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale (AIS) grade, upper extremity motor score (UEMS) and total motor score (TMS), lower extremity motor score (LEMS), light touch and pinprick sensory scores, Spinal Cord Independence Measure (SCIM), and Short Form-36 (SF-36) domains at baseline and follow-up were analyzed with regression models adjusted for age and sex. Overall recovery across TMS, SCIM, and SF-36 Physical Component Summary was analyzed with an O'Brien-style global statistical test (GST). Interactions tested whether bridge metrics modified riluzole's effect. At baseline, greater ventral ( β = 9.65, p = 0.017) and total ( β = 6.16, p = 0.021) tissue-bridge widths were associated with higher TMS, and ventral width with higher UEMS ( β = 6.61, p = 0.010). Larger dorsal (odds ratio [OR] = 21.92, p = 0.013), ventral (OR = 4.91, p = 0.049), and total (OR = 3.70, p = 0.019) bridges corresponded to less severe baseline AIS grade. Pinprick scores increased with ventral ( β = 26.56, p = 0.020) and total ( β = 17.50, p = 0.023) bridge width, and light touch scores increased with total bridge width ( β = 16.22, p = 0.045). No imaging metric was associated with LEMS. These individual-metric associations were nominally significant but did not survive correction. In GST analyses, larger ventral ( T = 4.63, p = 0.012, p '= 0.048) and total ( T = 4.30, p = 0.019, p '=0.048) bridges predicted greater overall recovery; both remained significant after correction and were stable across sensitivity analyses. Ventral and total bridge width showed nominally significant interactions with riluzole treatment for upper-limb motor recovery. Exploratory DTI findings were inconclusive and sensitive to individual observations: both the FA-recovery association and the observation of poor outcome despite a preserved tissue bridge rested on a single participant. Overall, we found that midsagittal tissue-bridge width measured ∼72 h after injury from standard-of-care T2-weighted MRI was associated with baseline injury severity and multidomain functional recovery, at a timepoint substantially earlier than the 1 month at which tissue bridges have previously been quantified. Because edema may obscure lesion margins this early, acute bridge widths may underestimate spared tissue resolvable later. The treatment-interaction observation is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective confirmation. These findings support MRI-derived tissue bridges as candidate biomarkers for prognostication and enrichment of neuroprotective trials in SCI.

title: A deep learning approach for brain tumor classification using hybrid efficient net and inception networks in MRI images.
abstract: BackgroundA brain tumor is a medical pathology, whereas biomedical imaging is a key element used to visualize the condition. Brain tumor classification is an essential imaging task for early pinpointing and treatment. Accurate and timely tumor characterization supports appropriate treatment planning, prognosis assessment and better patient outcomes.ObjectiveThis paper aims to develop an efficient hybrid deep learning model for early detection of brain tumors from MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) images.MethodsTo classify tumors, this work proposes a hybrid EfficientNet B7 and Inception V4 (ENETV4) network. The Inception network interprets spatial features for improving classification accuracy, while the EfficientNet B7 framework increases the computational efficiency to maintain high feature extraction ability. A unified feature is created by concatenating the retrieved features from the two models. To improve classification performance, a Figshare dataset comprising glioma, meningioma and pituitary tumor MRI images was used. Optimized hyperparameters enhanced generalization across the 70:20:10 train-test-validation split of the multi-sequence MRI dataset.ResultsThe proposed hybrid ENETV4 networks achieved 98.53% accuracy using an independent dataset, outperforming existing methods when evaluated on the dataset. These results accurately differentiate various kinds of tumors. This paper compares the hybrid ENETV4 model with the traditional models, reaffirming that the hybrid ENETV4 method enables effective classification of brain tumors from medical images, helping clinicians select suitable treatment strategies.ConclusionThe proposed hybrid methods provide accurate tumor classification in an early stage, supporting timely clinical decisions and treatment planning.

title: AI- assisted compressed sensing for accelerated 1.5T shoulder MRI.
abstract: BackgroundShoulder MRI has relatively long acquisition times. The clinical performance of AI-assisted compressed sensing (ACS) acceleration levels in 1.5-T shoulder MRI remains unclear.ObjectiveTo compare the acquisition time, image quality, and diagnostic agreement of three clinical shoulder MRI protocols using parallel imaging (PI), ACS4, and ACS8 at 1.5 T.Materials and MethodsProspectively, 158 patients with shoulder discomfort underwent three scanning protocols-the conventional Parallel imaging (PI) protocol, the ACS with a nominal acceleration factor of 4 (ACS4), and the ACS with a nominal acceleration factor of 8 (ACS8), covering four common sequences. Acquisition time, quantitative image quality parameters including True SNR, Relative SNR, Relative CNR, and edge rising distance (ERD), subjective image quality scores from three radiologists, and diagnostic agreement in an exploratory subgroup of 25 patients were assessed.ResultsACS4 and ACS8 reduce the total acquisition time by approximately 29% and 45%, respectively, compared with the PI protocol while maintaining comparable image quality across evaluated sequences. ACS8 generally demonstrated higher quantitative Relative SNR/CNR values in several tissues and sequences, whereas ACS4 achieved the highest True SNR and subjective image quality scores. ERD differences were not statistically significant, and diagnostic agreement was generally high across protocols.ConclusionACS protocols reduced acquisition time in 1.5-T shoulder MRI, although ACS8 compromised subjective image quality. ACS4 offered a more favorable balance between scanning efficiency and image quality.

title: Riesz-Quincunx WaVnet Chaotic Rime Attention Encoder and ensemble convolutional neural networks for remote brain tumor diagnosis.
abstract: BackgroundAccurate classification and segmentation of brain tumors from medical images are essential for reliable diagnosis and treatment planning. However, variations in image quality, noise, and tumor characteristics can complicate automated analysis.ObjectiveThis study aims to develop a deep learning framework for the accurate classification and segmentation of brain tumors by integrating an ensemble convolutional neural network (CNN) with the Riesz-Quincunx WaVnet Chaotic Rime Attention Encoder.MethodsThe proposed framework incorporates image preprocessing techniques to enhance contrast, reduce noise, and improve image quality. The ensemble CNN is integrated with the Riesz-Quincunx WaVnet Chaotic Rime Attention Encoder to strengthen feature extraction and representation. The framework is designed to identify brain abnormalities and classify tumor subregions, including necrotic tumor cores, enhancing tumors, peritumoral edematous areas, and non-enhancing tumor cores. Furthermore, a Flask-based web application is developed to facilitate remote access and support clinical collaboration.ResultsThe proposed framework is designed to improve brain tumor classification and segmentation by combining ensemble learning with enhanced feature representation. However, quantitative performance metrics are required to substantiate its diagnostic accuracy, segmentation performance, and superiority over existing methods.ConclusionThe proposed deep learning framework integrates image preprocessing, ensemble CNN classification, and attention-based feature extraction to support automated brain tumor analysis. Its Flask-based deployment offers potential for remote accessibility and telemedicine applications, supporting medical specialists in diagnostic decision-making. Further validation using quantitative performance metrics and independent clinical datasets is necessary to establish its clinical reliability.

title: A review of medical image segmentation research based on bibliometrics.
abstract: BackgroundMedical image segmentation is a fundamental step in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning, and its research landscape has expanded rapidly with the advancement of artificial intelligence. A systematic bibliometric overview of this field is therefore needed to clarify its intellectual structure and emerging trends.ObjectiveTo provide a comprehensive bibliometric overview of the global research landscape, developmental trends, collaboration networks, and emerging hotspots in the field of medical image segmentation over the past decade.MethodsA bibliometric analysis was performed on 21,437 publications related to medical image segmentation, indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection from 2016 to 2025. The analysis systematically examined publication outputs, country-level contributions, author collaboration networks, journal distributions, and keyword co-occurrence patterns.ResultsThe annual publication count increased remarkably from 25 in 2016 to 5,207 in 2025. China contributed the largest share with 11,556 publications, followed by the United States (3,272) and India (1,924). Core researchers formed stable intra-team collaborations, though inter-team cooperation remained limited. Keyword and citation analyses identified deep learning, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Transformers, U-Net, and their variants as dominant methodological themes. Case studies on skin and lung segmentation revealed differential research attention and international collaboration patterns across anatomical targets. A historical trajectory analysis showed methodological evolution from traditional image processing to fully convolutional networks and U-Net, and subsequently to hybrid architectures integrating attention mechanisms and Transformers.ConclusionMedical image segmentation has experienced substantial growth, driven by deep learning innovations. Future research may increasingly focus on multimodal foundation models capable of generalizable segmentation across diverse clinical scenarios. This bibliometric review offers researchers a valuable reference for understanding the intellectual structure and frontiers of the field.

title: Federated Learning: Envisioning a Pathway to More Accessible and Equitable Cleft Care.
abstract: Cleft lip and palate represents the most common congenital craniofacial anomaly worldwide, with low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) bearing nearly 84% of the global disease burden. Despite the instrumental role of global nongovernmental organizations (NGOs) in expanding access to cleft care across LMICs, patient databases and healthcare infrastructure remain highly fragmented across centers and organizations. Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning hold considerable promise for improving cleft care through data-driven clinical decision-making. However, privacy regulations present significant barriers to the centralized aggregation of patient data required to train robust artificial intelligence models. Federated learning (FL) offers a potential solution by enabling multiple institutions to train a shared global model without transferring raw patient data to a central server. Through mechanisms such as federated averaging, differential privacy, and homomorphic encryption, FL substantially mitigates privacy risks while producing models that perform comparably to models trained on centralized pool data. Existing implementations, most notably the Federated Tumor Segmentation initiative spanning 71 institutions across 6 continents, demonstrate the feasibility of this approach in complex healthcare settings. This narrative review proposes a potential framework for applying FL to global cleft care, outlining how existing organizational infrastructure established by prominent cleft NGOs can provide a foundation for a federated network. Five key stakeholder categories: global cleft NGOs, academic medical centers, technology partners, funding entities, and local cleft centers have been identified as essential to realizing this vision. Numerous challenges and barriers have also been identified before realizing this endeavor.

title: Ectopic Prostate Tissue Within the Seminal Vesicle: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: IntroductionEctopic prostate tissue confined to the seminal vesicle is an exceptionally rare congenital genitourinary anomaly. Its presentation as a grossly identifiable, mass-forming lesion constitutes an even rarer clinicopathological entity that is almost universally misdiagnosed preoperatively. Given the extreme rarity of this condition, no consistent diagnostic criteria or standardized management protocols have been established.Patient PresentationWe describe a 75-year-old asymptomatic man in whom a pelvic cystic mass was incidentally discovered during a routine health check-up. Preoperative pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) suggested a benign cystic lesion arising from the right seminal vesicle, and the patient subsequently underwent an uncomplicated laparoscopic resection. The gross specimen consisted entirely of a well-circumscribed nodular lesion that had been completely enucleated from the seminal vesicle parenchyma; no adjacent seminal vesicle tissue was submitted for pathological evaluation. Immunohistochemical analysis confirmed the mass as ectopic, hyperplastic prostatic tissue within the right seminal vesicle, with positive staining for prostate-specific antigen (PSA), NKX3.1, and intact basal cell layers, while the seminal vesicle marker PAX8 was negative.ConclusionThis lesion lacks specific clinical and imaging features, and a definitive diagnosis can only be rendered through histopathological evaluation combined with a targeted immunohistochemical panel. Complete surgical excision confers an excellent long-term prognosis. Heightened clinical awareness of this entity is essential to avoid misdiagnosis and unnecessary intervention.

title: Tractography-Based Insights into Neuroplasticity and Clinical Heterogeneity in Parkinson's Disease Subtypes.
abstract: Parkinson's disease shows substantial heterogeneity across motor, cognitive, and non-motor domains, reflecting variable patterns of neurodegeneration and compensation across distributed brain circuits. Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) tractography enables pathway-specific characterization of white-matter alterations and provides a framework for linking clinical subtypes to tract-level patterns that may be obscured by skeleton-based or connectomic averaging. Here, we synthesize white-matter evidence across motor, cognitive, genetic, and prodromal dimensions of PD heterogeneity, using tractography as an organizing framework within a broader dMRI and multimodal context. We review diffusion approaches ranging from diffusion tensor imaging to free-water, neurite, and fixel-based models. We distinguish pathway reconstructions from other diffusion and imaging analyses and consider how complementary approaches inform, but do not uniquely determine, interpretations of degeneration and subtype-specific neuroplasticity. Emerging methods, including harmonization pipelines, radiomic tractometry, and machine learning classifiers, may further improve tract-level sensitivity and reproducibility. Cognitive subtypes illustrate how posterior association and limbic tract degeneration, together with cholinergic and noradrenergic dysfunction, shape clinical progression. Integrating tractography with molecular, genetic, functional, and clinical markers may support subtype-specific biomarkers for risk stratification, prognosis, and targeted neuromodulation or rehabilitation strategies, although longitudinal and external validation is required before routine use.

title: Multimodal neuroimaging in Alzheimer's disease: A practical, case-illustrated review of quantitative MRI and molecular PET.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) accounts for 60-70% of dementia cases worldwide. Current diagnostic pathways rely on structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to exclude secondary causes, amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) to confirm pathology, and tau PET for disease staging. However, these approaches are limited by subjectivity, cost, accessibility, and variability in interpretation. Quantitative imaging tools such as volumetric MRI and NeuroQuant offer reproducible metrics that may enhance diagnostic precision and standardization. This review synthesizes literature published between 2000 and 2026 evaluating structural MRI, quantitative volumetric MRI, amyloid PET, tau PET, FDG PET, and emerging adjunctive imaging techniques, supplemented by illustrative clinical cases demonstrating multimodal integration in practice. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of NeuroQuant in standardized atrophy quantification and its integration with molecular imaging modalities. Volumetric MRI enhances PET-based diagnosis and staging by contextualizing amyloid and tau pathology within patterns of selective neurodegeneration. Quantitative metrics correlate with cognitive decline and disease progression. Multimodal imaging strategies improve diagnostic specificity, longitudinal monitoring, and phenotypic stratification across the AD. Multimodal imaging provides a comprehensive framework for AD management. Quantitative MRI using NeuroQuant bridges structural and molecular domains, supporting standardized assessment and integration with emerging precision diagnostic approaches.

title: Passive Sealing Stent-Grafts for Chimney Endovascular Repair: In Vitro Examination and a Japanese Single-Centre Retrospective Study.
abstract: Purpose Juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms (JAAAs) present with a short infrarenal neck that does not permit standard endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). The AFX VELA cuff extension with its endoskeletal architecture may reduce type Ia endoleak (TIaEL) through passive sealing. We examined this hypothesis using a double-chimney benchtop model and a clinical cohort treated with VELA-based chimney EVAR (ChEVAR). Materials and methods A benchtop model compared gutter leakage volumes among VELA, Endurant II and Excluder C3 (5 trials per device). A retrospective single-centre cohort (January 2018-April 2024) included consecutive JAAA patients undergoing VELA-based ChEVAR with ≥12-month follow-up. Postoperative computed tomographic (CT) morphometry compared seal-zone geometry across the 3 platforms. Results In the benchtop model, VELA showed a median gutter leakage of 5.0 mL/min (interquartile range [IQR], 4.0-11.0), whereas both comparators exceeded 500 mL/min and were right-censored. In the clinical cohort, 20 patients (55% male; median age 80.0 years) underwent ChEVAR for JAAAs with a median diameter of 53.5 mm and infrarenal neck length of 5.0 mm. Clinically successful sac exclusion was achieved in 19 of 20 patients (95%). Intraoperative TIaEL occurred in 5 patients: 1 major endoleak was sealed with adjunctive gutter coil embolisation, and 4 minor endoleaks resolved spontaneously on the 1-month CT angiogram. Over a median follow-up of 36.5 months, no persistent TIaEL was detected on follow-up imaging, and no chimney stent-graft (SG) occlusion occurred. One patient (5%) required an aortic-related reintervention for a type Ib endoleak. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decreased by ≥20% in 9 patients (45%), and 1 started dialysis at 4 years. On postoperative CT morphometry, relative gutter area was lowest with VELA, intermediate with Endurant II and highest with Excluder C3; circumferential apposition followed the inverse pattern. Conclusion In the benchtop model, VELA produced consistently lower leakage than both comparators, with concordant CT morphometric evidence consistent with a passive sealing mechanism. In this cohort, VELA-based ChEVAR achieved clinically successful sac exclusion in 19 of 20 patients (95%) with no persistent TIaEL and no chimney SG occlusion. These findings support the feasibility of VELA-based ChEVAR when FEVAR is unavailable; multicentre prospective validation is required. Clinical impact Persistent type Ia endoleak (TIaEL) is a principal limitation of chimney EVAR (ChEVAR) compared with fenestrated EVAR (FEVAR). We report short-to mid-term outcomes of ChEVAR using the AFX VELA cuff extension, whose endoskeletal architecture is designed to promote passive sealing. Postoperative CT morphometry comparing the 3 devices (VELA, Endurant II and Excluder C3) showed a smaller relative gutter area and higher circumferential apposition with VELA, paralleling the benchtop pattern. VELA-based ChEVAR achieved clinically successful sac exclusion in 19 of 20 patients (95%), without persistent TIaEL detected on follow-up imaging. VELA-based ChEVAR appears feasible when FEVAR is unavailable; however, multicentre validation is required.

title: Bilateral Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis Deployment With IVUS-Guided Contrast-Sparing Technique: A Complex Case Report.
abstract: Background Preserving internal iliac artery (IIA) patency during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for aortobiiliac aneurysms typically requires substantial contrast volume, posing risk to patients with renal insufficiency. Case description We present the case of an elderly female with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3b (baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate 35 mL/min/1.73 m², serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL) and an aortobiiliac aneurysm who underwent complex bilateral iliac side-branch (iliac branch endoprosthesis [IBE]) deployment. The procedure used intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) as the primary guidance to minimize contrast exposure. A notable intraoperative challenge arose on the left side, where retrograde cannulation was unsuccessful due to anatomical tortuosity and sheath dislodgement. We therefore performed a left axillary cut-down, which facilitated successful IIA reconstruction and resolved a type 1b endoleak. The total contrast volume employed was approximately 38 mL. Incidental findings included hyperthyroidism and suspected lymphoproliferative disorder. Conclusion Intravascular ultrasound-guided bilateral IBE is feasible and substantially reduces contrast exposure in patients with renal impairment, though technical flexibility is essential for complex anatomy.Clinical ImpactIVUS-guided bilateral iliac branch endoprosthesis deployment may offer a contrast-sparing option for patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing endovascular repair of complex aortobiiliac aneurysms. Using IVUS for vessel identification, sizing, landing-zone selection, and stent-apposition assessment can reduce reliance on iodinated contrast while preserving internal iliac artery perfusion. This case shows that bilateral reconstruction is feasible with only 38 mL of contrast, even when complex anatomy requires axillary access. Its innovation is using IVUS as the primary guidance modality, with angiography reserved for confirmation and troubleshooting.

Background

Preserving internal iliac artery (IIA) patency during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for aortobiiliac aneurysms typically requires substantial contrast volume, posing risk to patients with renal insufficiency.

Case description

We present the case of an elderly female with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3b (baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate 35 mL/min/1.73 m², serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL) and an aortobiiliac aneurysm who underwent complex bilateral iliac side-branch (iliac branch endoprosthesis [IBE]) deployment. A notable intraoperative challenge arose on the left side, where retrograde cannulation was unsuccessful due to anatomical tortuosity and sheath dislodgement. We therefore performed a left axillary cut-down, which facilitated successful IIA reconstruction and resolved a type 1b endoleak. The total contrast volume employed was approximately 38 mL. Using IVUS for vessel identification, sizing, landing-zone selection, and stent-apposition assessment can reduce reliance on iodinated contrast while preserving internal iliac artery perfusion. This case shows that bilateral reconstruction is feasible with only 38 mL of contrast, even when complex anatomy requires axillary access. Its innovation is using IVUS as the primary guidance modality, with angiography reserved for confirmation and troubleshooting.

title: Successful Management of Infective Native Infrarenal Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Associated With Micrococcus luteus and Streptococcus mitis in a 77-year-Old Man.
abstract: BackgroundInfected native abdominal aortic aneurysm (INAAA) is a rare but life-threatening condition characterized by rapid progression and high mortality.Case SummaryWe report a 77-year-old male with a history of arterial hypertension, ischemic heart disease, and stage IVB hormone-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma, presenting with lumbar pain and mild inflammatory activation, including leukocytes 8.8 ×10³/µL and C-reactive protein 3.6 mg/dL (normal <0.50 mg/dL). Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrated a 50-mm infrarenal aneurysm, with periaortic inflammatory changes and a periaortic hematoma. A multidisciplinary decision, made 3 hours after admission, favored urgent open surgical repair with resection and in situ reconstruction. Midline laparotomy with debridement and resection of the affected aorta was performed; in situ reconstruction was carried out using a rifampicin soaked bifurcated Dacron graft covered with bovine pericardium with anastomoses to healthy aortic and iliac segments. Intraoperative cultures identified Micrococcus luteus and Streptococcus mitis , rare pathogens in this context. Targeted therapy included intravenous ceftriaxone during hospitalization, followed by oral amoxicillin-clavulanate and doxycycline for seven weeks. Histopathology confirmed chronic granulomatous abscessed inflammation. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged home on postoperative day 17. At six months, follow-up imaging demonstrated a patent reconstruction without signs of persistent infection.ConclusionThese findings highlight the importance of early recognition, aggressive debridement, and coordinated multidisciplinary management in achieving optimal outcomes in INAAA, particularly when atypical microorganisms complicate diagnosis and therapeutic decision-making.

title: Do we classify and treat consistently? A retrospective, two-centre observer agreement study of Neer classification and treatment selection for proximal humerus fractures.
abstract: Background The Neer classification is widely used for proximal humerus fractures, but its reproducibility and relation to treatment remain uncertain. This retrospective, two-centre observer agreement study evaluated interobserver and intraobserver agreement and the association between Neer category and treatment recommendation. Methods Forty eligible fractures from two institutions were evaluated twice by 12 observers, approximately 3 months apart. Observers received age, sex and deidentified plain radiographs, assigned a Neer classification, and selected treatment. Agreement was assessed using Gwet coefficients and Cohen kappa; mixed-effects logistic regression evaluated factors associated with treatment selection. Results Interobserver agreement for Neer classification was moderate at both rounds (AC2, 0.470 at T0 and 0.507 at T1). No significant differences in classification agreement were detected across experience groups. Neer classification was associated with operative treatment and, among operative recommendations, arthroplasty rather than osteosynthesis (both p < 0.001). Each 10-year age increase was independently associated with higher odds of arthroplasty versus osteosynthesis (adjusted odds ratio, 4.44; 95% confidence interval, 2.30-8.56; p < 0.001). Discussion Neer classification showed moderate reproducibility and was associated with treatment selection. Greater classification agreement among shoulder specialists was not demonstrated, although experience group comparisons were not separately powered. Increasing Neer complexity and older age were associated with treatment choice.

title: Unilateral Biportal Endoscopy Versus Percutaneous Endoscopic Interlaminar Discectomy for Highly Migrated Lumbar Disc Herniation: A Retrospective Comparative Study With Quantitative MRI-Based Decompression Analysis.
abstract: Study designRetrospective comparative cohort study.ObjectiveTo compare the perioperative, clinical, and radiographic outcomes of unilateral biportal endoscopy (UBE) and percutaneous endoscopic interlaminar discectomy (PEID) in the treatment of highly migrated lumbar disc herniation (HMLDH).MethodsA total of 128 patients with single-level HMLDH who underwent UBE (n = 63) or PEID (n = 65) between June 2022 and January 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. All patients completed a minimum follow-up period of 2 years. Perioperative variables, complications, and reoperation events were analyzed. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Radiographic decompression was quantitatively assessed using the postoperative dural sac cross-sectional area (DSCA) expansion rate measured on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).ResultsCompared with PEID, UBE was associated with a significantly shorter operative time, less endoscopic hemostasis time, and lower fluoroscopy time. Intraoperative blood loss was lower in the PEID group. Early postoperative back pain was significantly lower in the PEID group, whereas no significant between-group differences were observed in long-term VAS or ODI outcomes. The overall complication rate was significantly lower in the UBE group. In addition, UBE achieved a significantly greater DSCA expansion rate and a lower rate of residual disc fragments than PEID.ConclusionUBE and PEID achieved comparable long-term clinical outcomes in patients with HMLDH. UBE demonstrated advantages in perioperative efficiency, radiographic decompression, and reduced radiation exposure. Furthermore, UBE was associated with a lower overall complication rate, primarily attributable to a lower incidence of postoperative nerve root irritation.

title: Evaluating Multimodal Vision Frontier Models for Grading Neuroforaminal Stenosis on Lumbar Spine MRIs.
abstract: Study DesignDiagnostic accuracy study.ObjectiveTo determine whether a general-purpose multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) model, Gemini 3 Pro, grades lumbar neuroforaminal stenosis on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in agreement with expert radiologists, particularly for severe stenosis, and whether a vertebral-level localizer overlay helps.MethodsOne hundred lumbar MRIs from the Radiological Society of North America (RSNA) 2024 Lumbar Spine Degenerative Classification Dataset, graded by expert radiologists, provided 1,000 foramina (five levels, both sides) labeled normal/mild, moderate, or severe. Sagittal and axial T2-weighted series were converted into short scrolling videos and submitted to the model with a structured grading prompt; no task-specific training was performed. The primary outcome was agreement with expert grades (linearly weighted Cohen's kappa, κw); secondary outcomes were accuracy, severe-stenosis sensitivity, direction of errors, and the localizer effect.ResultsAgreement with expert grading was poor (κw 0.20, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.14-0.26). Accuracy was 70.6% (95% CI 67.7-73.4) but reflected the 70.4% of foramina that were normal/mild. The model identified 17.9% of severe foramina (95% CI 8.9-30.4) and called 58.9% normal/mild. Errors were systematically toward undergrading (p < 0.001). The localizer did not improve accuracy (70.0% vs 70.6%, p = 0.590) and reduced severe sensitivity (3.6% vs 17.9%, p = 0.043).ConclusionsWithout task-specific training, a general-purpose AI model reached moderate accuracy only because most foramina were normal or mild; it missed most severe stenosis and systematically undergraded. In its current form this approach is unsuitable for screening, triage, operative decision-making, or independent report generation.

title: Subcutaneous Basal Cell Carcinoma of the Cheek: A Diagnostic Pitfall.
abstract: Background Subcutaneous basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is a rare subtype of BCC. We present a case of primary deep-seated BCC on the cheek to highlight the diagnostic challenges and surgical management of this atypical presentation. Case presentation A 58-year-old male with no history of skin malignancy presented with a subcutaneous cheek mass. Excisional biopsy revealed BCC involving the deep soft tissue with positive deep margins for residual tumour. Management and findings The patient subsequently underwent a formal re-excision and received adjuvant radiotherapy. Histopathology confirmed an infiltrative growth pattern within the subcutaneous fat. The patient was lost to follow-up following adjuvant radiotherapy. Conclusions This case underscores the importance of considering BCC in the differential diagnosis of subcutaneous facial masses. The proposed histogenesis is either that of a deep follicular or sebaceous unit origin. For plastic surgeons, achieving clear deep margins is paramount to preventing recurrence in these rare and occult presentations.

title: Comparison of emergency department-measured optic nerve sheath diameter according to early neurological outcome in pediatric patients with traumatic brain injury.
abstract: Background Early risk stratification in pediatric traumatic brain injury (TBI) is challenging, and readily available bedside markers may help identify children at risk of an adverse clinical course. This study compared emergency department (ED)-measured optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) and related ocular ultrasound measurements according to early neurological outcome in children with TBI. Methods This perspective observational study was conducted at Mardani-Azar Pediatric Medical Center, Tabriz, Iran, between January and December 2025. Children younger than 18 years with TBI underwent ocular ultrasonography during their ED evaluation. Bilateral ONSD, eyeball transverse diameter (ETD), and interocular distance (IOD) were measured, and the ONSD/ETD and ONSD/IOD ratios were calculated. Neurological status was assessed 3-5 days after admission using the Glasgow coma scale (GCS). Associations between ultrasound measurements and early clinical outcomes were evaluated using between-group comparisons and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results Among 100 patients, 84 patients (84%) had no CT findings suggestive of raised ICP, whereas 16 patients (16%) had at least one such finding. Mean ONSD was higher in the unfavorable-outcome group than in the favorable-outcome group (5.84 ± 0.67 vs. 4.55 ± 0.41 mm; P < 0.001). The ONSD/ETD and ONSD/IOD ratios were also higher in the unfavorable-outcome group (both P < 0.001), whereas ETD and IOD did not differ significantly. Mean ONSD showed an area under the ROC curve of 0.961 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.913-0.994) for discriminating the study-defined outcome groups. Conclusion ED-measured ONSD was associated with early neurological status in this pediatric TBI cohort. These findings suggest that ONSD may warrant further evaluation as an adjunctive bedside risk-stratification marker. Prospective validation using standardized outcome definitions and appropriate adjustment for initial injury severity is needed before its independent prognostic value can be established. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: An explainable multimodal model integrating post-ESD mucosal defect images and clinical features to predict delayed bleeding after colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection.
abstract: Background Existing tools for predicting delayed bleeding (DB) after colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) use only structured clinical variables, leaving information in post-ESD mucosal defect images unused. We developed and externally validated an explainable multimodal model integrating these images with clinical features. Methods We retrospectively included 3,416 patients who underwent colorectal ESD at two hospitals from January 2022 through June 2026 (development cohort, n = 2,778; external validation cohort, n = 638). DB was active bleeding 6 h to 28 days after ESD, confirmed by repeat endoscopy and requiring endoscopic hemostasis. YOLOv11m-seg segmented mucosal defects, ResNet50 generated an image-derived prediction score (E-Score), and the E-Score was fused with clinical features. After LASSO feature selection, five algorithms with and without SMOTE were evaluated by fivefold stratified cross-validation. SHAP and Grad-CAM provided post-hoc feature- and image-level explanations. Results DB occurred in 224 patients (8.06%) in the development cohort and 53 (8.31%) in the external validation cohort (P = 0.839). The segmentation model achieved mAP50 and mAP50-95 values of 0.984 and 0.838. Six features were retained. XGBoost without SMOTE (PrismDB) performed best (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC], 0.804; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.769-0.837), with 64.73% sensitivity, 85.40% specificity, and 96.50% negative predictive value. In external validation, the AUC was 0.788 (95% CI, 0.724-0.850), sensitivity was 79.25%, specificity was 83.25%, and negative predictive value was 97.79%. Probability calibration in the development cohort under the natural event distribution showed a calibration slope of 1.101 and an intercept of + 0.227 (Brier score, 0.0584). E-Score had the highest mean absolute SHAP contribution, and representative activation maps overlapped with exposed vessels, adherent clots, and eschar. Conclusions PrismDB showed stable discrimination for DB after colorectal ESD. Low-risk classification did not exclude DB. Probability calibration was acceptable in the development cohort but has not been evaluated externally, and the safety of model-guided changes to postoperative care remains to be established; the companion web application demonstrates the prediction workflow.

title: Influence of dominant sequence artifacts on generative AI for virtual contrast-enhancement in breast MRI.
abstract: Background Virtual contrast-enhanced (vCE) breast MRI is a deep learning approach for generating contrast-like images from non-contrast acquisitions. As diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) has emerged as a major contributor to enhancement synthesis, understanding the influence of DWI-related image artifacts is important for the robustness and potential clinical implementation of AI-based contrast-free imaging approaches. We evaluated the robustness of a pix2pix-based vCE synthesis model to artifact-contaminated DWI during training and inference. Materials and methods This IRB-approved, retrospective study included 1,974 multiparametric breast MRI examinations (mean age: 49 years) acquired with two clinical routine 3T MRI scanners (2017-2022). High b-value (b = 1500 s/mm 2 ) DWI images were automatically classified for high-intensity (HI) and low-intensity (LI) artifacts using a pretrained neural network. A pix2pix 2D-GAN was trained either after excluding artifact-affected slices (vCE-clean) or using all available slices (vCE-all). Performance was evaluated using image similarity metrics, lesion-based analysis, reader assessment, and correlation of artifact scores with reconstruction errors. Results Excluding artifact-affected slices during training resulted in a small but statistically significant increase in whole-image structural similarity index (SSIM) with small effect size (vCE-all 0.843 ± 0.034; vCE-clean 0.849 ± 0.031, p < 0.001, d av = 0.20). However, lesion-based metrics and qualitative ratings of lesion enhancement and image quality were comparable between models. During Inference, strong LI DWI artifacts were associated with higher lesion-based errors. Conclusion Controlling for artifacts on diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) during vCE training only minorly influenced technical metrics but not perceived image quality/lesion enhancement. In contrast, severe signal-loss artifacts during inference impaired local performance, highlighting the importance of image quality control during potential deployment.

title: Comparative evaluation of handheld vs. high-end ultrasound systems for TIPSS hemodynamic assessment: first impressions.
abstract: Background Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPSS) procedures require reliable post-interventional hemodynamic monitoring to detect shunt dysfunction, for which Doppler ultrasonography is the preferred modality. Owing to the rapid development of handheld ultrasound devices, their diagnostic equivalence to high-end systems warrants investigation. Materials and methods A pilot group of 23 patients (n = 13 males, 65%; n = 7 females; 35%; n = 3 unknown) with intrahepatic TIPSS were retrospectively analyzed. Blood flow measurements were obtained and compared using a high-end ultrasound system (Resona R9, Mindray) and modern handheld ultrasound device (Vscan Air™ CL, GE). The TIPSS was evaluated using B-mode and color Doppler sonography. Image quality was assessed using a 5-point scale and flow parameters using statistical analysis. The image quality and the difference between the two devices were analyzed using correlation coefficients and multivariable linear regression models including TIPSS flow values, skin-to-TIPSS distance, and TIPSS dwell time. Results Both devices produced clinically interpretable images. However, the high-end device yielded superior image quality in 16 of 23 cases (p < 0.001). Significant correlations were observed between the difference in mean TIPSS flow measurements obtained by the two devices (Δ mean TIPSS flow) and corresponding average flow values measured by the two devices (Kendall's τ = 0.656; p < 0.001). Significant associations with Δ TIPSS mean flow were identified for skin-to-TIPSS distance (τ = 0.39; p = 0.014) and TIPSS dwell time (τ = -0.39; p = 0.017). In multivariable analysis, both mean TIPSS flow measured by the high-end system and skin-to-TIPSS distance remained significantly associated with Δ TIPSS mean flow. The TIPSS mean flow measured by the high-end system correlated with TIPSS dwell time (τ = 0.38; p = 0.021). Bland-Altman analysis revealed that handheld measurements tended to overestimate low flows and underestimate high flows. Conclusion Handheld ultrasound devices show promising potential for TIPSS surveillance; however, they could lead to distorted flow deviations. Contemporary handheld devices may nevertheless be useful in selected point-of-care settings but cannot yet replace high-end systems for precise hemodynamic monitoring. Larger prospective studies are required. originalAbstract:
Background

Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPSS) procedures require reliable post-interventional hemodynamic monitoring to detect shunt dysfunction, for which Doppler ultrasonography is the preferred modality. Owing to the rapid development of handheld ultrasound devices, their diagnostic equivalence to high-end systems warrants investigation.

Materials and methods

A pilot group of 23 patients (n = 13 males, 65%; n = 7 females; 35%; n = 3 unknown) with intrahepatic TIPSS were retrospectively analyzed. Blood flow measurements were obtained and compared using a high-end ultrasound system (Resona R9, Mindray) and modern handheld ultrasound device (Vscan Air™ CL, GE). The TIPSS was evaluated using B-mode and color Doppler sonography. Image quality was assessed using a 5-point scale and flow parameters using statistical analysis. The image quality and the difference between the two devices were analyzed using correlation coefficients and multivariable linear regression models including TIPSS flow values, skin-to-TIPSS distance, and TIPSS dwell time.

Results

Both devices produced clinically interpretable images. However, the high-end device yielded superior image quality in 16 of 23 cases (p < 0.001). Significant correlations were observed between the difference in mean TIPSS flow measurements obtained by the two devices (Δ mean TIPSS flow) and corresponding average flow values measured by the two devices (Kendall's τ = 0.656; p < 0.001). Significant associations with Δ TIPSS mean flow were identified for skin-to-TIPSS distance (τ = 0.39; p = 0.014) and TIPSS dwell time (τ = -0.39; p = 0.017). In multivariable analysis, both mean TIPSS flow measured by the high-end system and skin-to-TIPSS distance remained significantly associated with Δ TIPSS mean flow. The TIPSS mean flow measured by the high-end system correlated with TIPSS dwell time (τ = 0.38; p = 0.021). Bland-Altman analysis revealed that handheld measurements tended to overestimate low flows and underestimate high flows.

Conclusion

Handheld ultrasound devices show promising potential for TIPSS surveillance; however, they could lead to distorted flow deviations. Contemporary handheld devices may nevertheless be useful in selected point-of-care settings but cannot yet replace high-end systems for precise hemodynamic monitoring. Larger prospective studies are required.

No clinical trial registration was performed, as this study is a single-center retrospective observational analysis based on existing clinical data. The study did not involve prospective patient enrollment, international procedures, or assignment to treatment groups. Therefore, registration in a clinical trial registry was not applicable.

title: Preoperative prediction of lymphovascular space invasion in early-stage cervical cancer using a deep learning-based 3D super-resolution MRI radiomics model.
abstract: Background Lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI) is a critical prognostic factor guiding adjuvant therapy in early-stage cervical cancer, yet its preoperative assessment is often limited by the spatial resolution of standard MRI. This study aimed to investigate the value of a deep learning-based 3D super-resolution (SR) MRI radiomics model in predicting LVSI and to evaluate how SR reconstruction impacts image quality and radiomic feature robustness. Methods This retrospective study included 117 patients with early-stage cervical cancer (training cohort: n = 81; validation cohort: n = 36). A 3D Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (SRGAN) reconstructed T2-SPAIR and DWI sequences into super-resolution images (SRI) with a 4× upsampling factor. Radiomic features were extracted, and an SRI-based multimodal fusion model was developed and systematically compared with original image (OI)-based and clinical models using the Area Under the Curve (AUC) and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA). Results SR reconstruction significantly improved the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for both DWI (P = 0.012) and T2-SPAIR (P = 0.030). For DWI, SRI preserved intratumoral texture heterogeneity, leading to improved diagnostic performance (Validation AUC: SRI-DWI 0.864 vs. OI-DWI 0.727, P = 0.041). The final SRI-Fusion model achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy (Validation AUC: 0.934), significantly outperforming the OI-Fusion model (AUC: 0.828, P = 0.044) and the clinical model (AUC: 0.626, P = 0.012). Conclusions SRGAN-based reconstruction effectively improves MRI quality and feature robustness, particularly in DWI. The SRI-based multimodal radiomics model demonstrates superior predictive performance for LVSI in early-stage cervical cancer compared to conventional imaging and clinical models.

title: Can radiomics outperform radiologists in predicting Ewing sarcoma response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy from longitudinal MRI?
abstract: Objective This retrospective, multicenter study evaluated whether MRI-based radiomics can predict the histological response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in Ewing sarcoma patients and compared their performance to that of radiological findings. Definitive histological assessment is only possible during surgery, potentially delaying therapy changes and increasing metastatic risk; therefore, a positive outcome would enable early adaptations. Methods Radiomics features were extracted from pre- and post-neoadjuvant (after first chemotherapy cycle) chemotherapy scans of patients treated from 2004 to 2020. Four machine learning models were trained using nested cross-validation to predict histological response, and their performance was compared to models trained on semantic features derived from expert radiological readings. Diagnostic performance was measured by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Results 96 patients (mean age, 19.9 ± 11.7 years; 41 women) with Ewing sarcoma were evaluated. Radiomics features related to low gray level intensity changes in T1 fat-saturated contrast-enhanced sequences showed the highest responder identification performance (AUROC, 0.62; 95% CI: 0.59, 0.65), surpassing the best radiological model, which relied on the relative change in maximum diameter of extratumoral soft tissue components (AUROC, 0.58; 95% CI: 0.56, 0.60). Radiomics models relying on pre-treatment T2-weighted data performed similarly (AUROC, 0.61; 95% CI: 0.58, 0.64), outperforming the clinical baseline (AUROC, 0.53; 95% CI: 0.51, 0.55). Conclusion MRI-based radiomics moderately identified responders to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, suggesting a role for earlier, tailored therapeutic strategies in Ewing sarcoma. Larger studies to validate these findings within a multimodal framework are warranted. Clinical relevance statement Radiomics extracted from MRI scans may aid with non-size tissue signals in early prediction of neoadjuvant chemotherapy response in Ewing sarcoma patients, potentially guiding personalized treatment adaptations, reducing delays for non-responders, and improving patient outcomes. These exploratory findings are complementary to standard size-based assessment from clinical routine, and warrant larger, prospective trials to be established.

title: Multimodal imaging features of atypical multifocal torpedo maculopathy: a case report.
abstract: Background Torpedo maculopathy (TM) is a rare congenital retinal abnormality, typically presenting as a solitary, torpedo-shaped hypopigmented lesion located temporal to the fovea with its apex pointing toward the fovea. Multifocal TM is exceedingly uncommon, and its multimodal imaging characteristics and lesion distribution remain incompletely understood. Case presentation A 32-year-old man was referred after an incidental abnormality was detected in the fundus of his right eye. He was asymptomatic, with uncorrected visual acuity of 20/20 in both eyes. Color fundus photography revealed a typical torpedo-shaped lesion temporal to the macula and additional elongated temporal lesions with indistinct borders. OCT demonstrated focal RPE attenuation or loss, increased choroidal hypertransmission, and outer retinal involvement, with a slit-like subretinal cleft in one lesion. FFA showed multiple well-demarcated hyperfluorescent lesions without leakage, whereas ICGA revealed corresponding hypofluorescent areas and provided clearer delineation of lesion margins and extent. These findings supported the diagnosis of atypical multifocal torpedo maculopathy. Given the absence of symptoms and preserved visual function, no treatment was required and periodic follow-up was recommended. Conclusions Multifocal TM may show atypical morphology on color fundus photography, with some lesions appearing poorly demarcated and their extent potentially underestimated. Integrated multimodal imaging, particularly OCT, FFA, and ICGA, enables a more comprehensive assessment of lesion morphology, distribution, and structural heterogeneity. Among these modalities, ICGA may provide additional value in delineating lesion boundaries and extent. This case further expands the imaging spectrum of multifocal TM and highlights the importance of integrated multimodal imaging in atypical presentations.

title: When a glabellar dermoid cyst is not the whole story: the significance of MRI in excluding intracranial segments.
abstract: Background Epidermoid and dermoid cysts are one of the most common benign pediatric tumors of the skull. Ultrasonography is usually the diagnostic tool of choice for their evaluation and diagnosis. Although benign, local growth with cosmetic issues, bone erosion, and occasional intracranial involvement generally warrant surgical resection. Since epidermoid and dermoid cysts may be seen by a wide range of medical disciplines, standardized recommendations for optimal diagnosis and treatment are necessary. Case presentation We report the case of a 14-month-old boy, who underwent neurosurgical removal of a glabellar dermoid cyst classified as an extracranial lesion, and in whom an intracranial lesion was identified on follow-up MRI, represents a rare and unusual clinical course. Ten months after surgery, a surveillance MRI revealed an intracranial lesion in the right frontal parasagittal region, while the child had developed no symptoms. Very careful retrospective review of the initial MRI suggested that an extremely small intracranial part of the lesion might have been faintly visible upon knowledge of the further clinical course. The intracranial lesion was subsequently resected and diagnosed as an epidermoid cyst. In our mini-review, we have compiled evidence that intracranial extension is more common than expected and particularly occurs in craniofacial midline lesions but is definitely not restricted to them. Conclusion Together, this case and literature review highlight the importance of careful preoperative assessment and interdisciplinary discussion to adequately determine the extent of craniofacial dermoid and epidermoid cysts before surgery. This case illustrates that a subtle intracranial lesion may not be recognizable on initial image interpretation despite MRI having been performed. Imaging follow-up is definitely recommended when intraoperative findings raise concern about deeper extension.

title: MRI-based assessment of greater tuberosity exposure in massive rotator cuff tears: a systematic review of current evidence and methodological gaps.
abstract: Background Massive rotator cuff tears (MRCTs) lack a standardized and reproducible imaging-based definition. A recent Delphi consensus introduced greater tuberosity exposure (GTE) as a defining criterion for MRCTs, proposing that MRCTs be classified by either involvement of at least two rotator cuff tendons or ≥ 67% GTE on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Purpose To evaluate the role of GTE in the MRI-based definition and structural characterization of MRCTs and to describe the extent and methodological maturity of the evidence available for GTE and established MRI-derived parameters. Methods A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from database inception to February 17, 2026, and updated on October 9 and 11, 2026 with supplementary citation searching, in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies were included if they investigated MRCTs using MRI-based or MRI-transferable imaging and reported structural definitions, measurement methods, or associations with irreparability, structural healing, or clinical outcomes. Prognostic studies were assessed using the Quality In Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool. Findings were synthesized narratively; no meta-analysis was performed due to substantial heterogeneity in study designs, imaging protocols, and outcome definitions. The synthesis described the extent and methodological maturity of the available evidence and did not compare diagnostic or prognostic performance between parameters. Results A total of 34 studies were included. No study evaluated GTE as a quantitative MRI-derived parameter. Only two studies addressed footprint coverage on imaging, one qualitatively and one by a semi-quantitative five-zone score of residual tendon attachment; neither measured GTE as a defined exposure parameter or applied predefined thresholds. In contrast, MRCTs were consistently characterized using indirect structural parameters, primarily tendon involvement and tear size. Established MRI-derived variables-including tear size, tendon retraction, fatty infiltration, muscle atrophy, and superior humeral migration-were assessed using established measurement frameworks based on defined anatomical landmarks, notwithstanding methodological heterogeneity in imaging protocols and thresholds across studies. These parameters were frequently evaluated in relation to irreparability, structural healing, and functional outcomes, whereas no study evaluated a direct quantitative MRI-based measure of GTE in relation to a clinical or structural endpoint. Conclusion No standardized and outcome-validated MRI-based method for quantifying GTE was identified within the scope of this review. Despite its conceptual appeal as a direct representation of footprint deficiency, GTE has not yet undergone standardized measurement development or outcome-based validation. The evidence base for established MRI-derived parameters is more extensive and methodologically mature, with operationalized measurement methods and reported outcome associations; this does not imply clinical inferiority of GTE. Future research should focus on developing reproducible MRI-based measurement techniques for GTE and evaluating its diagnostic and prognostic relevance in dedicated validation studies. Study design Systematic review; Level of evidence, 3. Individual included studies ranged from Level II to Level V.
